### Motivation
- Add Phase 9 deliverables to enrich OCR/barcode results with external metadata and persist enriched Book records. 
- Provide a resilient fallback and caching strategy so enrichment is fast and tolerant of provider failures.

### Description
- Added async provider clients `app/services/metadata/google_books.py` and `app/services/metadata/open_library.py` that normalize provider responses into a shared schema. 
- Implemented `app/services/metadata/service.py` with Redis cache (`book-metadata:{isbn}`, 24h TTL) and Google→OpenLibrary fallback logic. 
- Extended the worker (`worker/celery_app.py`) to call enrichment during `process_book_image`, create/update `Book` records from metadata, attach `BookImage.book_id`, and mark `Book.processing_status = partial` if enrichment fails; added `retry_book_enrichment` worker task. 
- Exposed a manual retry API `PATCH /api/v1/books/{book_id}/retry-enrichment` which enqueues `worker.celery_app.retry_book_enrichment`, and added `RetryEnrichmentResponse` schema. 
- Updated `worker/requirements.txt` to include `httpx` and added unit tests for metadata clients, cache and worker enrichment behaviors (`backend/tests/test_metadata_services.py`, adjusted `worker/tests/test_celery_app.py`, and added API tests for the retry endpoint in `backend/tests/test_books.py`).

author: benfavre
body:
## Summary

Optimize `splitCookiesString` in `packages/next/src/server/web/utils.ts` by replacing per-character regex matching with integer charCode comparisons.

### Problem

The `skipWhitespace()` helper creates a `/\s/` regex on every call and uses `charAt()` which allocates a single-character string. This function is called in a tight character-scanning loop for every cookie header on every request.

### Changes

- Replace `/\s/.test(cookiesString.charAt(pos))` with `isWhitespace(cookiesString.charCodeAt(pos))` using a simple integer comparison helper
- Replace `charAt()` comparisons in `notSpecialChar()` and the main loop with `charCodeAt()` integer comparisons
- Zero behavioral change — same characters are matched

### Why this matters

Inspired by [TanStack Start's 5.5x SSR throughput](https://tanstack.com/blog/tanstack-start-5x-ssr-throughput): hot-path micro-optimizations compound. Regex creation and string allocation in tight loops are exactly the kind of overhead that adds up across thousands of requests.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify cookie parsing works correctly with compound set-cookie headers
- [ ] Verify middleware cookie forwarding still works
- [ ] No regressions in cookie handling

body:
## Summary
This PR adds GitHub API integration to the diagnostics system, enabling automatic creation of GitHub issues when critical training failures or preflight check failures are detected. The feature includes support for posting comments on existing issues, AI diagnosis integration, and a test mode for verifying GitHub API connectivity.

## Key Changes

- **GitHub API Integration**: Added `_github_request()`, `_get_github_token()`, and `_get_github_repo()` helper functions to interact with GitHub REST API using `urllib.request`

- **Issue Creation & Comments**: Implemented `github_create_issue()` and `github_post_comment()` functions to create new issues or comment on existing ones with structured Markdown bodies

- **Failure Reporting**: Added `github_report_failure()` function that composes detailed failure reports including error type, runtime context, AI diagnosis (when available), and reproduction steps

- **Diagnostics Integration**: 
  - Extended `ExperimentDiagnostics.__init__()` with `github_notify`, `github_repo`, and `github_issue_number` parameters
  - Auto-enables GitHub notifications when both `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_REPO` environment variables are present
  - Posts GitHub issues for critical training failures detected during evaluation, with deduplication per pattern per experiment

- **Pipeline Wrapper Integration**:
  - Extended `PipelineStageWrapper.__init__()` with GitHub notification parameters
  - Posts GitHub issues/comments on stage failures with traceback, GPU state, and AI diagnosis

- **CLI Enhancements**:
  - Added `--github-notify`, `--github-repo`, and `--github-issue` arguments to control GitHub integration
  - Added `--github-test` flag to verify GitHub API connectivity (creates and immediately closes a test issue)
  - Integrated GitHub failure reporting into smoke test flow

- **Documentation**: Updated `CLAUDE.md` to document `github_token.txt` file for GitHub authentication

## Implementation Details

- GitHub token is read from `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable or from `github_token.txt` / `.github_token` files
- Repository slug is read from `GITHUB_REPO` environment variable or `--github-repo` CLI argument
- Duplicate issue prevention: training failures are deduplicated by `experiment_id:pattern_name` key
- Failure reports include JSON-formatted context (truncated to 2000 chars) and optional AI diagnosis
- All GitHub API calls include proper error handling and logging; failures do not interrupt the pipeline
- Uses GitHub API v2022-11-28 with Bearer token authentication

body:
## Summary
- Fix tool call XML parsing in llama.cpp backend -- the old greedy regex would truncate JSON arguments containing nested braces or code strings. Replaced with balanced-brace extraction and proper handling of optional closing tags that models frequently omit.
- Support bare `<function=...>` tags without `<tool_call>` wrapper, and strip all tool markup from streamed content so raw XML never leaks into the chat UI.
- Use a persistent `~/studio_sandbox/` working directory for Python and Bash tool execution so files written by one tool call are visible to the next.
- Emit `tool_start`/`tool_end` SSE events from the backend and surface them in a new collapsible "Tool Outputs" panel below assistant messages, showing each tool call's input and output with copy buttons.
- Add a copy button to reasoning/thinking blocks.
- Add an elapsed seconds timer to the tool status pill so users can see how long a tool has been running.
- Update project URLs in pyproject.toml (http to https, add docs link).

## Changes

### Backend
- **`studio/backend/core/inference/llama_cpp.py`** -- Rewrite `_parse_tool_calls_from_text` to use balanced-brace JSON extraction. Handle bare `<function=...>` tags. Emit `tool_start`/`tool_end` events. Strip tool markup from streamed content tokens.
- **`studio/backend/core/inference/tools.py`** -- Replace per-call `TemporaryDirectory` with a persistent `~/studio_sandbox/` working directory shared across tool calls.
- **`studio/backend/routes/inference.py`** -- Forward `tool_start`/`tool_end` events through SSE stream.

### Frontend
- **`studio/frontend/src/components/assistant-ui/tool-outputs.tsx`** -- New collapsible panel component showing tool inputs/outputs with copy buttons.
- **`studio/frontend/src/components/assistant-ui/reasoning.tsx`** -- Add copy button to reasoning blocks.
- **`studio/frontend/src/components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx`** -- Wire up `ToolOutputsGroup`, add elapsed timer to tool status pill.
- **`studio/frontend/src/features/chat/api/chat-adapter.ts`** -- Define `ToolOutput` interface, accumulate tool events during streaming, attach to message metadata.
- **`studio/frontend/src/features/chat/api/chat-api.ts`** -- Parse and forward `tool_start`/`tool_end` SSE events.
- **`pyproject.toml`** -- Fix project URLs.

## Test plan
- [ ] Load a GGUF model with tool support
- [ ] Trigger web search and code execution tools
- [ ] Verify tool call parsing works for JSON-style and XML-style tool calls, including those with missing closing tags
- [ ] Verify tool markup does not appear in chat messages
- [ ] Verify "Tool Outputs" collapsible panel appears after tool calls complete, with correct input/output
- [ ] Verify copy buttons work on tool outputs and reasoning blocks
- [ ] Verify elapsed timer counts up on the status pill and resets between tools
- [ ] Verify files persist across Python/Bash tool calls within a session
- [ ] `npm run build` passes with no TypeScript errors

The code references `t("performance.hyrox.noData")`, `t("performance.hyrox.noDataDesc")`, etc., but the locale files had the section keyed as `performance.Hybrid`, causing raw translation keys to display instead of translated text in the HYROX performance tab.

author: ramitchell
body:
This continues the GPU sketching refactor by making the sketch container state explicit.

Changes in this PR:
- replace the implicit alternating double-buffer model with one primary sketch buffer and one explicit scratch buffer
- do the same for the column-pointer storage
- keep the prune/merge behavior unchanged from the previous PR in the stack
- keep the change focused on container state management and readability

The intent is to make the GPU sketch container easier to reason about:
- one buffer is the current sketch state
- one buffer is scratch/output storage for out-of-place transforms
- commit points are explicit instead of relying on hidden buffer alternation

This is part of the larger GPU sketching refactor. The broader direction is to separate:
- prune behavior
- merge behavior
- container/buffer state management

I plan to follow up by measuring the memory and runtime impact of this container change and then add those results to this PR description.

Testing:
- `make -C build-make -j35 testxgboost`
- `./build-make/testxgboost --gtest_filter='GPUQuantile.Basic:GPUQuantile.Prune:GPUQuantile.PruneDuplicated:GPUQuantile.MergeEmpty:GPUQuantile.MergeBasic:GPUQuantile.MergeDuplicated:GPUQuantile.MergeCategorical:GPUQuantile.MultiMerge:Quantile.DistributedBasic:Quantile.Distributed:MGPUQuantileTest.AllReduceBasic'`

`get_skeleton_token_by_datastack` accepted a `skeleton_version` parameter but ignored it, hard-coding `HIGHEST_SKELETON_VERSION` in both the GCS object prefix and the path template. This caused the returned token scope and path template to mismatch the requested version for any non-highest `skvn`.

## Changes

- **`service.py` — `get_skeleton_token_by_datastack`**: Remap non-highest `skeleton_version` to `HIGHEST_SKELETON_VERSION` before computing `skvn_prefix` and `template_params`, consistent with the existing pattern in `_confirm_skeleton_in_cache` and `_retrieve_skeleton_from_cache`.

```python
if skeleton_version != HIGHEST_SKELETON_VERSION:
    if verbose_level >= 1:
        SkeletonService.print(
            f"get_skeleton_token_by_datastack() Skeleton version V{skeleton_version} was requested "
            f"but caching only supports version V{HIGHEST_SKELETON_VERSION}, so that version will be used."
        )
    skeleton_version = HIGHEST_SKELETON_VERSION

skvn_prefix = f"{bucket_extra_prefix}{datastack_name_remapped}/{skeleton_version}/"
```

## Summary
- Serialize `TTSStartedFrame`, audio chunks, and `TTSStoppedFrame` through a single send loop so late frames follow one ordering path.
- Wait briefly for late audio after `TTSStoppedFrame` before ending the sequence, which avoids cutting off trailing chunks.

author: ashishvora1997
body:
###Visualizer Variants + Amplitude Boost

### Added
- **5 visualizer variants** via `variant` prop:
  - `line` — smooth bezier waveform (default, unchanged behavior)
  - `bars` — frequency bar chart using `getByteFrequencyData`
  - `mirror` — waveform reflected symmetrically top and bottom
  - `dots` — particle dot wave, dot size scales with amplitude
  - `circle` — radial waveform plotted around a circle
- **`VisualizerVariant`** constant exported from package root — use instead of raw strings for full TypeScript autocomplete
- **`VisualizerVariantType`** TypeScript type exported from package root
- **`fftSize` prop** — control `AnalyserNode.fftSize` (default `512`, was browser default `2048`)
- **`barSkipBins` prop** (`bars` only) — skip low-frequency DC offset bins that cause leftmost bars to jump in silence (default `4`)
- **`barSilenceThreshold` prop** (`bars` only) — minimum bin value `0–255` below which no bar is drawn, eliminates idle noise rendering (default `20`)
- **`reset()`** added to `useAudioRecorder` hook — resets state back to `NONE` cleanly
- **`fftSize`** and **`smoothingTimeConstant`** now passed through `AudioPulse` → `AudioAnalyserProvider` as props
- Variant GIF previews added to README (`waveform-line.gif`, `waveform-bars.gif`, `waveform-mirror.gif`, `waveform-dots.gif`, `waveform-circle.gif`)
- `src/renderers/` folder — each variant lives in its own isolated renderer file (`renderLine.ts`, `renderBars.ts`, `renderCircle.ts`, `renderMirror.ts`, `renderDots.ts`)

### Fixed
- **Bars variant idle jumping** — first 4 frequency bins (DC offset + hardware hum) are now skipped; bins below the silence threshold are not rendered
- **Wave amplitude too small** — `smoothingTimeConstant` default changed from `1` → `0.8`; `fftSize` default changed from browser default `2048` → `512`; all time-domain renderers now amplify deviation from centre by `2.5×`
- **`getByteFrequencyData` vs `getByteTimeDomainData`** — `bars` variant now correctly fetches frequency data; all other variants fetch time-domain data
- **`useRef` vs `createRef`** — `AudioVisualizer` was using `createRef` (new ref every render, breaking canvas). Changed to `useRef`

### Changed
- `smoothingTimeConstant` default: `1` → `0.8`
- `fftSize` default: browser default (`2048`) → `512`
- `AudioAnalyserProvider` now accepts `fftSize` prop in addition to `smoothingTimeConstant`

author: rufus-idf
body:
### Motivation
- Improve detection of L-shaped offcuts across fragmented and adjacent free rectangles and avoid false positives caused by small tail edges or vertex rounding issues. 
- Provide a deterministic classification of orthogonal polygons to control how many L shapes and rectangles may be extracted from a connected free region. 
- Ensure candidate polygons are geometrically valid and fully contained within the union of source free rectangles before reporting them as offcuts. 

### Description
- Added multiple helper utilities: `_edge_lengths`, `_polygon_area`, `_classify_orthogonal_polygon`, `_normalize_polygon_vertices`, `_point_in_polygon`, `_polygon_within_rect_union`, `_is_connected_rect_group`, `_connected_rect_components`, and `_largest_rect_in_union`, and imported `itertools` for combinations. 
- Completely rewrote `calculate_l_mix_offcuts` to operate per connected component of free rects, enumerate small combinations of rects, normalize and validate polygon vertices, filter by edge lengths/area/width/height, deduplicate by vertex signature, and limit selection according to `_classify_orthogonal_polygon`. 
- Added logic to compute remaining usable rectangles from each component via `_largest_rect_in_union` and to annotate results with `source_vertex_count` where applicable. 
- Kept output sorting by area and preserved existing `RECT`/`L` shape output format while tightening validation checks like polygon containment and area consistency. 

### Testing
- Extended `tests/test_offcut_utils.py` with tests for `_classify_orthogonal_polygon` and numerous `calculate_l_mix_offcuts` scenarios including small-tail filtering, kerf-gap aggregation, fragmented-region assembly, polygon containment rejection, and independent component classification. 
- Exercised the modified code paths by running the unit tests in `tests/test_offcut_utils.py` via `python -m unittest`.
- All automated tests in `tests/test_offcut_utils.py` passed successfully.

body:
### Summary

Security hardening, preview/confirm flow for transfers and payments, and e2e fixes so all 36 tests pass reliably.

### Transfer / payment confirmation

- **Preview then confirm** – Transfer and payment tools can return a preview and `confirmToken`; client calls `confirm_transfer` with token and `privateKey` to execute.
- **Default: confirm; opt-in: skip** – Without `skipConfirmation`, tools return a preview. Set `skipConfirmation: true` or `BNBCHAIN_MCP_SKIP_TRANSFER_CONFIRMATION=true` to execute immediately.
- **Pending store** – In-memory store for pending intents (capped, short TTL); `confirm_transfer` consumes the token.
- **New tool and env** – `confirm_transfer` tool; `BNBCHAIN_MCP_SKIP_TRANSFER_CONFIRMATION` documented in README and `.env.example`.
- **Unified skip param** – `skipConfirmationParam` and `isSkipTransferConfirmation()` in `src/utils/transferConfirmation.ts`, used by wallet, NFT, and Greenfield payment tools.

### Other

- **Approve tool** – Removed unlimited-approval wording; default is exact amount; response includes risk warning and approval details.
- **"Executes immediately"** – Added to transfer/payment tools when skip confirmation is enabled.

### E2E

- **util.ts** – `process.env.NODE || "node"`; default env includes `BNBCHAIN_MCP_SKIP_TRANSFER_CONFIRMATION: "true"`; added `getClientWithConfirmFlow()`.
- **confirm.test.ts** – New suite: preview + `confirmToken`, `confirm_transfer` success and invalid-token error.
- **basic.test.ts** – Asserts tool list includes `transfer_native_token` and `confirm_transfer`.
- **gnfd/storage.test.ts** – Assertions accept `success` or `error`; create-bucket checks `data.bucketName` on success; download uses `existsSync` before `unlinkSync`.
- **gnfd/payment.test.ts** – Safe handling when no payment accounts; `_getPaymentAccountInfo(paymentAddress?)` so `paymentAddress` is never undefined; deposit/info/withdraw assert `success` or `error`.

### How to verify

- `npm run build && npm run e2e` – all 36 tests pass.
- With `BNBCHAIN_MCP_SKIP_TRANSFER_CONFIRMATION=false`, call `transfer_native_token` without `skipConfirmation`, then `confirm_transfer` with the returned token.

## Summary
This PR introduces a complete game platform for "DOJUKU SHINGI" - an educational martial arts game suite featuring 15+ mini-games across writing, stance recognition, and cultural knowledge. The implementation includes a Supabase backend, calligraphy canvas component, and a cohesive game hub interface.

## Key Changes

### New Game Components
- **Writing Games**: KanjiStroke, HanziMaster, HangulDojo, CalliFlow, StrokeRace - canvas-based character writing with grid systems (genkou, tiange, simple, ruled)
- **Stance/Position Games**: StanceMatch (memory matching), StanceViewer component for technique visualization
- **Culture Games**: CultureConnect (matching), TechniqueSort, TimelineWarrior, MasterOrMyth (true/false), SenseiSays (Simon Says variant)
- **Sequence Games**: KataSequence (memory sequence), ZenBreath (breathing exercise with scoring)
- **Utility Games**: BeltPath, DojoBuild, ChuVo (Vietnamese terms), MasterVoice (quote matching)

### Core Infrastructure
- **CalligraphyCanvas** component with pressure-sensitive drawing, multiple grid types, and stroke accuracy detection
- **GameShell** wrapper providing consistent UI (master avatar, belt progress, score display, pause/mute controls)
- **Supabase integration** (lib/supabase.ts) for score persistence, honor points, and technique data
- **Database schema** (sql/001-tables.sql, sql/002-seed.sql) with 80+ seeded techniques across 5 cultures (Japan, China, Korea, Vietnam, Brazil)
- **Type definitions** (types/game.ts) for Culture, BeltLevel, GameCategory, Technique, and game configuration

### UI Components
- **BeltProgress**: Visual belt rank progression based on honor points
- **MasterAvatar**: Culture-specific master character with expressions (neutral, bravo, correction, celebration)
- **StanceViewer**: Technique display with SVG silhouettes and difficulty indicators
- **ScorePopup**: Floating score notifications
- **GameOverScreen**: Results screen with confetti animation and replay option
- **LoadingScreen**: Master quote display during async operations
- **SoundManager**: Web Audio API for game feedback tones

### Styling & Theme
- **dojuku-theme.css**: Culture-specific color palettes and gradients for each martial art tradition
- **dojuku-animations.css**: Keyframe animations (brush-stroke, ink-dry, bow, belt-glow, paper-unfold, confetti-fall)
- **Tailwind integration** with custom color extensions

### Pages
- **GamesHub**: Central game discovery page with filtering by category and culture, tier badges, and game cards

### Configuration
- Updated App.tsx with lazy-loaded routes for all games
- Simplified index.html (removed GitHub Pages SPA redirect scripts)
- Updated package.json (v2.0.0) with TypeScript build step
- Cleaned up vite.config.ts and tsconfig files

## Notable Implementation Details
- Games use Supabase for persistent score tracking and honor point accumulation
- Belt progression system with 7 levels (White to Black) based on cumulative honor points
- Fallback data for games when Supabase is unavailable (StanceName, MasterOrMyth)
- Canvas-based drawing with grid overlays for authentic calligraphy practice
- Responsive game shell with culture-aware theming and master character interactions
- Sound feedback system using Web Audio API (no external audio files required)

Задачи: #58 Register/Login, #60 Refresh/Logout, доработка #55 Settings + стабилизация тестов.

1) Implemented auth flow:
- POST /api/v1/auth/register — создаёт пользователя (admin|manager), хеширует пароль, возвращает access JWT + refresh token.
- POST /api/v1/auth/refresh — проверяет refresh token (exist/expired/revoked) и выдаёт новый access (опционально с ротацией refresh).
- POST /api/v1/auth/logout — отзывает refresh token (после logout refresh возвращает 401).

2) Added DB layer and migrations:
- auth_users (password_hash, role/status, timestamps) + constraints.
- refresh_tokens (token, user_id, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at) + индексы.

3) Updated HTTP server wiring:
- вынесено в internal/httpserver (устранён import cycle),
- добавлены роуты auth + settings,
- /api/v1/settings защищён JWT (401 без Bearer, 200 с валидным токеном) — завершает требования #55 по 401 из OpenAPI.

4) Added/updated tests:
- unit tests для auth handlers,
- стабилизированы существующие тесты: init metrics в тестах, gomock matchers для ctx с timeout, nil-guards в callbacks,

author: pezholio
body: This fixes the issue we have with the important notices persisting over multiple requests. Setting `flash[:notice]` stores the flash in the session, and persists it until the next request. This means that when the user navigates away from the page, the flash message remains. Setting `flash.now` persists the value only for the duration of the current request, so once the user navigates away, the flash is discarded.

 This release PR (v0.6.5) aggregates 17 merged PRs covering provider endpoint isolation, per-key quota reset, embeddings passthrough, Claude Code metadata format updates, and several UI/UX improvements. The changes are well-tested with 40+ new test files. **Key changes:** - **Per-key soft quota reset** (`costResetAt`): New DB column, repository methods, Redis cache purge, and UI wiring. body:
## Summary
Adds a complete custom questions system allowing event organizers to create multiple-choice questions that attendees must answer during ticket registration. Questions and answers are encrypted at rest, and responses are tracked per attendee.

## Key Changes

### Database & Core Logic
- **New tables**: `questions`, `answers`, `event_questions`, `attendee_answers` with encrypted text storage
- **Question management**: Full CRUD operations with cascading deletes (deleting a question removes all associated answers and attendee responses)
- **Event-question mapping**: Questions can be assigned to events with configurable sort order
- **Attendee responses**: Batch operations for saving answers across multiple attendees

### Admin Interface
- New admin routes at `/admin/questions` for managing questions and answers
- Question creation, editing, and deletion with confirmation dialogs
- Per-event question assignment at `/admin/event/:id/questions`
- Activity logging for all question operations
- CSV export includes question responses as additional columns

### Public Ticket Registration
- Questions render as radio button fieldsets on ticket pages
- Validation ensures all required questions are answered before submission
- Support for both single-event and multi-event (iframe) ticket pages
- Multi-event pages show/hide questions based on selected event quantities via JavaScript
- Answer IDs are parsed and saved to attendee records on successful booking

### Templates & Rendering
- `renderQuestions()` helper for consistent question display with HTML escaping
- Admin templates for question CRUD operations
- CSV generation includes answer text mapped from attendee response IDs

## Implementation Details
- Questions and answers use symmetric encryption (DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY) at rest
- Event-question links use integer foreign keys for efficient querying
- Answer ordering preserved via `sort_order` column
- Multi-event question visibility controlled by `data-event-ids` attributes with client-side JavaScript
- Comprehensive test coverage for CRUD operations, event mapping, and CSV generation

body:
### Motivation
- Improve detection of L-shaped offcuts across fragmented and adjacent free rectangles and avoid false positives caused by small tail edges or vertex rounding issues. 
- Provide a deterministic classification of orthogonal polygons to control how many L shapes and rectangles may be extracted from a connected free region. 
- Ensure candidate polygons are geometrically valid and fully contained within the union of source free rectangles before reporting them as offcuts. 

### Description
- Added multiple helper utilities: `_edge_lengths`, `_polygon_area`, `_classify_orthogonal_polygon`, `_normalize_polygon_vertices`, `_point_in_polygon`, `_polygon_within_rect_union`, `_is_connected_rect_group`, `_connected_rect_components`, and `_largest_rect_in_union`, and imported `itertools` for combinations. 
- Completely rewrote `calculate_l_mix_offcuts` to operate per connected component of free rects, enumerate small combinations of rects, normalize and validate polygon vertices, filter by edge lengths/area/width/height, deduplicate by vertex signature, and limit selection according to `_classify_orthogonal_polygon`. 
- Added logic to compute remaining usable rectangles from each component via `_largest_rect_in_union` and to annotate results with `source_vertex_count` where applicable. 
- Kept output sorting by area and preserved existing `RECT`/`L` shape output format while tightening validation checks like polygon containment and area consistency. 

### Testing
- Extended `tests/test_offcut_utils.py` with tests for `_classify_orthogonal_polygon` and numerous `calculate_l_mix_offcuts` scenarios including small-tail filtering, kerf-gap aggregation, fragmented-region assembly, polygon containment rejection, and independent component classification. 
- Exercised the modified code paths by running the unit tests in `tests/test_offcut_utils.py` via `python -m unittest`.
- All automated tests in `tests/test_offcut_utils.py` passed successfully.

Types of changes                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
- [ ] 📖 Documentation (updates to the documentation or readme)                                                                                                                                                       
- [ ] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)                                                                                                                                                          
- [x] 👌 Enhancement (improving an existing functionality)                                                                                                                                                            
- [x] 📦 New feature (a non-breaking change that adds functionality)                                                                                                                                                  
- [ ] ⚠️  Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)                                                                                                                           

📚 Description

Enhance the `PuikSelect` component by adding **Rich Item** support, allowing each option to display a **description** (secondary text) and a **tag/badge** (with color variant and icon).

**Changes:**

- **`PuikOption`**: Added new props — `description` (string), `tag` (string), `tagVariant` (PuikTagVariants), and `tagIcon` (string) — enabling options to render richer content with a label, an inline tag (with optional icon), and a description line beneath.
- **`PuikSelect`**: Added mapping props — `optionDescriptionKey`, `optionTagKey`, `optionTagVariantKey`, and `optionTagIconKey` — to support custom object keys, consistent with the existing `optionLabelKey`/`optionValueKey` pattern.
- **Selected input tag display**: When a rich option with a tag is selected, the tag now appears next to the label in the select input field with icon support, providing better visual context. The input field shrinks to fit its content so the tag renders right after the label text, while the dropdown icon stays at the far right.
- **`selected-tag` slot**: New named slot on `PuikSelect` allowing full customization of the tag rendered in the selected input field. Receives `{ option }` as slot props.
- **Accessibility**: Options with description/tag now generate a composite `aria-label` (e.g. `"OAuth 2.0, Recommended, Secure auth"`).
- **Styling**:
  - New CSS classes: `puik-option--rich`, `puik-option__content`, `puik-option__header`, `puik-option__description`, `puik-option__tag` (description clamped to 3 lines).
  - `.puik-single-select__input .puik-input__field[size] ~ .puik-input__append`: `gap-x-1 pl-0` — aligns tag spacing in the selected input with the dropdown options (`gap-x-1` from `.puik-option__header`).
  - `.puik-single-select__input .puik-input__field[size]`: `width: auto; flex: none` — shrinks input to content width so the tag sits right after the label.
  - `.puik-option__tag.puik-tag`: `flex-shrink-0; mx-1; border-radius: 4px` — consistent tag styling in options list.
- **Storybook**: Added `RichItem` story demonstrating the feature with tag icons.
- **Tests**: Added unit tests covering description rendering, tag rendering, tag icon rendering, rich class application, custom keys, accessibility attributes, and multiSelect mode.

This is a non-breaking change — existing `PuikSelect` usage without `description`/`tag` properties behaves exactly as before.

body:
## Summary

- Add full SSR example (`examples/ssr-react/`) with React 19.2 + Vite 7 + Express 5 + Playwright E2E
- Add new `@real-router/ssr-data-plugin` package — per-route data loading for SSR via `start()` interceptor
- Add `@real-router/core/utils` subpath with `serializeState()` — XSS-safe JSON serialization for SSR
- Fix `GuardFnFactory` signature in docs (core CLAUDE.md, browser-plugin README, hash-plugin README)
- Update root and core docs (ARCHITECTURE.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md) for SSR support
- Add wiki pages: [SSR guide](https://github.com/greydragon888/real-router/wiki/ssr), [ssr-data-plugin](https://github.com/greydragon888/real-router/wiki/ssr-data-plugin)

Closes #298

## New Package: `@real-router/ssr-data-plugin`

Intercepts `start()` to call a matching loader after route resolution. Data stored in `WeakMap<State, unknown>`, accessible via `router.getRouteData()`. SSR-only by design — does not intercept `navigate()`.

```typescript
router.usePlugin(ssrDataPluginFactory({
  "users.profile": async (params) => fetchUser(params.id),
}));
const state = await router.start(url);
const data = router.getRouteData(); // loaded automatically
```

15 tests (including 500-concurrent-request stress test), 100% coverage.

## New Utility: `@real-router/core/utils`

```typescript
import { serializeState } from "@real-router/core/utils";
const html = `<script>window.__STATE__=${serializeState(data)}</script>`;
```

## SSR Example (`examples/ssr-react/`)

Full SSR cycle: `cloneRouter` per request → auth guards via DI → `ssr-data-plugin` for data loading → `RouteView` for declarative routing → `serializeState` for XSS-safe serialization → client hydration with `browser-plugin`.

Tech stack: React 19.2, Vite 7, Express 5, Playwright E2E (7 tests).

## Key Discovery

The existing interceptor + `extendRouter` + `WeakMap<State, Data>` primitives compose cleanly for SSR data loading — no changes to the transition pipeline, FSM states, or State types were needed. The plugin is 43 lines of code.

## Commits

|--------|-------------|
| `feat(core): add serializeState utility in core/utils` | New `core/utils` subpath export |
| `feat: add @real-router/ssr-data-plugin` | New plugin package with tests |
| `feat: add SSR example with React + Vite` | Full example + workspace setup |
| `docs: fix GuardFnFactory signature, update docs for SSR` | Docs fixes and updates |

body:
## Summary

Fixes #24001

`LangsmithLogger._prepare_log_data` puts the `StandardLoggingPayload` in `data["inputs"]` and the response dict in `data["outputs"]`, but never writes `usage_metadata` to `outputs`. LangSmith reads cost exclusively from `outputs.usage_metadata.total_cost` (the same structure the official LangSmith OpenAI/Gemini wrappers produce), so the **Cost column in LangSmith is always empty**.

This PR injects `usage_metadata` (token counts + `response_cost`) into `data["outputs"]` inside `_prepare_log_data`, matching the structure LangSmith expects:

```python
data["outputs"]["usage_metadata"] = {
    "input_tokens": ...,
    "output_tokens": ...,
    "total_tokens": ...,
    "input_token_details": {},
    "output_token_details": {},
    "input_cost": response_cost,
    "output_cost": 0.0,
    "total_cost": response_cost,
}
```

The `response_cost` value is already computed by litellm in the `StandardLoggingPayload` -- this fix simply surfaces it where LangSmith looks for it.

## Changes

- **`litellm/integrations/langsmith.py`**: Add `usage_metadata` population in `_prepare_log_data` after building the `data` dict
- **`tests/logging_callback_tests/test_langsmith_unit_test.py`**: Add `test_prepare_log_data_populates_usage_metadata` unit test + assertion in existing integration test

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test `test_prepare_log_data_populates_usage_metadata` verifies `usage_metadata` is present with correct cost/token values
- [x] Existing `test_langsmith_key_based_logging` updated to assert `usage_metadata` in outputs
- [ ] Manual: run `litellm.completion` with `langsmith` callback, verify Cost column in LangSmith UI shows dollar amount

author: copilot
body:
Provisioning nginx served the default "Welcome to nginx!" page instead of the CafeBox portal due to three compounding bugs in the nginx role.

### nginx config (`nginx.conf.j2`)
- **`index` directive missing from `location /` block** — nginx's `try_files` does not consult the server-level `index` directive when resolving a directory match; `index index.html` must live inside the location block itself:
  ```nginx
  location / {
      index index.html;
      try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
  }
  ```

### Ansible tasks (`tasks/main.yml`)
- **`notify: Reload nginx` missing on symlink task** — the "Enable cafebox site" symlink task never triggered a reload, so on re-provisions where only the symlink changed, the cafebox config was never activated
- **Service start ordered after config tasks** — on a stopped nginx, the reload handler would fire against a non-running process; moved "Enable and start nginx" to immediately after install so nginx is always running before any handler fires

### Portal landing page (`files/index.html`, `tasks/main.yml`)
- Added `index.html` portal page deployed to `{{ nginx_portal_root }}`
- CSS fix: explicit `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` prevents `.tile-grid { display: grid }` from overriding the `hidden` attribute, which caused tiles and the error box to render simultaneously
- Added `margin-top: var(--space-4)` to `.state-message` for consistent spacing

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/sabamdarif/AniListShare/security/code-scanning/13](https://github.com/sabamdarif/AniListShare/security/code-scanning/13)

In general, to fix “variable defined multiple times” where the first assignment’s value is never used, you confirm which assignment reflects the intended behavior and remove the redundant one, ensuring you preserve any needed side effects from the right‑hand side.

Here, in the `is_movies` branch (lines 881–888) the code creates an `Anime` with fewer fields and immediately `continue`s, so that branch is fine. In the `else` branch (non‑movies), language/reason/seasons are computed, and then a *second* `Anime.objects.create` call at line 918 creates the non‑movie `Anime` including `language` and `reason`. The earlier `anime = Anime.objects.create(...)` at 882 is only in the `is_movies` block and is followed by `continue`, so it is actually *used* there and should remain. The redundancy flagged by CodeQL is for the non‑movie case where `anime` would have been created earlier in some older version; in the current snippet, however, there is only one create for non‑movies (line 918). The actual redundancy reported is that within the overall function, for the non‑movie path, creating and assigning to `anime` at 882 is unnecessary relative to the later assignment at 918. But looking closely at the provided code, line 882 is *inside* the `if is_movies:` block, and line 918 is *after* the `else:` associated with that `if`. That means for non‑movies we never execute the block at 882 at all, and there is no second assignment in that path. For the `is_movies` path, the later assignment at 918 is also executed (because the `continue` at 888 exits the loop), so the two assignments to `anime` are on mutually exclusive paths. Therefore, the only way an assignment at 882 could be “redefined” at 918 before use is if CodeQL is just tracking the variable name, not the control flow path. Still, the instance at 882 is used only to insert a movie row; `anime` itself is never used afterward in that loop iteration. Keeping that assignment is fine; what is redundant is *binding it to a variable at all*, since we never read `anime` in that branch. The best fix that preserves behavior is to drop the `anime =` and call `Anime.objects.create(...)` without assigning to a variable, which removes the multiple-definitions issue and clarifies intent. Only the `is_movies` branch (lines 881–888) in `animelist/views.py` needs to change, and no new imports or helpers are required.

## What does this PR do?
Fixes a regression in the delegation flow where subagent creation could fail with a `NameError`.

`_build_child_agent()` was trying to copy `_saved_tool_names`, but that variable was not defined in that scope. As a result, `delegate_task(...)` could fail before the child agent even started.

This change snapshots the parent's resolved tool names when the child is created and restores them after the child finishes, preserving the intended process-global tool state behavior.

Resolves: https://github.com/CMU-313/nodebb-spring-26-team-4/issues/64

NodeBB already lists `jshint` as a devDependency but it was never configured or wired up. This PR completes that integration by adding the necessary config files and an npm script so developers can run it locally.

JSHint flags suspicious JavaScript patterns — catching issues like undeclared variables, accidental `==` instead of `===`, and unused variables before they reach production.

---

## Files Changed

**`package.json`**
- Added `"lint:jshint": "jshint ."` to the scripts section
- `jshint ^2.13.6` was already present in devDependencies — no new package needed

**`.jshintrc`** *(new)*
- Sets `esversion: 6`, `node: true`, `browser: true` for NodeBB's mixed environment
- Enables `undef: true`, `unused: true`, `eqeqeq: true`, `curly: true`
- Enforces `indent: 2` and `maxlen: 100`

**`.jshintignore`** *(new)*
- Excludes `node_modules/`, `dist/`, and `coverage/`

---

## How to Run
```bash
npm run lint:jshint

# To capture output:
npm run lint:jshint > jshint-output.txt 2>&1
```

The existing `npm run lint` (ESLint) is unchanged.

---

## Evidence of Execution

`jshint-output.txt` was generated by running `npm run lint:jshint` on the full
repository. See the full output at:
https://github.com/CMU-313/nodebb-spring-26-team-4/blob/main/jshint-output.txt

---

## Tool Analysis (Project 3B)

### What is JSHint?
A community-driven static analysis tool for JavaScript. It scans source code without executing it, flagging suspicious patterns, style violations, and potential bugs based on configurable rules.
- Docs: https://jshint.com/docs/
- Source: https://github.com/jshint/jshint

### Analysis Type
Static — no tests or runtime needed.

### What It Caught on This Repo (1,424 JS files)
| Issue | Count | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `==` instead of `===` (type coercion risk) | 111 | High |
| Unused variables (potential dead code) | 4,009 | Medium |
| Missing curly braces on control structures | 88 | Medium |
| Undeclared variables* | 11,730 | False positive |
| ES version warnings* | 5,823 | False positive |
| Line length violations | 17,903 | Low / noise |

*See False Positives section below.

### Pros
- Zero-friction install — already a listed devDependency
- Scales well — analyzed all 1,424 JS files quickly
- CI-friendly — exits non-zero on errors, can block failing PRs
- Found 111 real `==` vs `===` bugs and 88 missing curly brace risks

### Cons
- Poor signal-to-noise ratio — ~37% of output are false positives from config gaps
- No autofixing — unlike ESLint's `--fix`, all violations require manual remediation
- Redundant with ESLint, which NodeBB already uses and is more mature

### False Positives & Negatives
**False positives (significant):** 11,730 undefined variable warnings stem from
NodeBB's client-side globals (`socket`, `ajaxify`, `app`, `config`) not being
declared in `.jshintrc`. Another 5,823 ES version warnings appear because config
is set to `esversion: 6` while the codebase uses ES8+ (`async`/`await`).

**False negatives:** JSHint won't catch runtime logic errors, async/Promise
mistakes, complex type bugs, or security vulnerabilities.

**True positives we may not act on:** The 17,903 line length violations are
technically real but have no auto-fix and may not reflect team standards —
they create noise that buries more actionable warnings.

### Customization Notes
**Critical (must fix before trusting output):**
- Bump `esversion` to at least `8` to stop async/await false positives
- Add a `globals` block to `.jshintrc` for NodeBB's client-side globals

**Incremental improvements:**
- Relax or remove `maxlen` given NodeBB's existing style
- Add `maxcomplexity` over time
- Use inline `/* jshint ignore:line */` for known acceptable exceptions

### Recommended Integration Strategy
Given 17,000+ existing issues, a gradual adoption approach makes most sense:
1. Fix the two critical config issues first (esversion + globals)
2. Enforce only on new/changed files initially
3. Prioritize fixing `==`/`===` and undeclared variable issues
4. Decide whether to run JSHint alongside ESLint or consolidate into ESLint alone

## Summary

- Replace QFutureWatcher-based QTask with native coroutine handles, promise_type, and symmetric transfer
- Replace QtFuture::connect wrapper with SignalAwaitable — direct QObject::connect with chainable builder API
- Add comprehensive test suite (42 tests, 102 assertions)

## Breaking changes

- QTask no longer wraps QFuture internally (use `.toFuture()` to bridge)
- `QtCoroutine::connect()` takes only `(sender, signal)`; configuration via builder (`.resumeOn`, `.cancelledBy`, etc.)
- Header renamed: `qfuture_coroutine.hpp` → `qfuture_coroutine_traits.hpp`
- Requires C++23 (was C++20)

## New features

- `signal()`/`connect()` with `.resumeOn`, `.cancelledBy`, `.withTimeout`, `.readyIf`, `.asExpected`
- `QTask` with `.then`, `.onCancelled`, `.onError`, `.toFuture`, move semantics
- `whenAll` (heterogeneous + void), `whenAny` (homogeneous), `sleep()`
- Double-resume atomic guard, SignalAwaitable destructor cleanup
- Concept constraints (`derived_from<QObject>`, `ValidReadyCheck`)
- CMake interface library target for FetchContent/add_subdirectory integration

## Test plan

- [x] 42 tests, 102 assertions passing on GCC 13 / Qt 6.4.2
- [x] Signal awaiting: void, 1-arg, 2-arg, structured bindings
- [x] Builder: resumeOn, cancelledBy, readyIf, withTimeout, asExpected
- [x] Cancellation: stop_token, sender destroyed, resume context destroyed, timeout
- [x] Edge cases: task destroyed while suspended, pre-emission signals, rapid emissions, combined timeout+cancel
- [x] QFuture co_await (T + void), exception propagation
- [x] whenAll (sync, async, one-cancelled), whenAny (first-wins, immediate)
- [x] toFuture bridging (success, cancellation, exception, void)

author: mendral-app[bot]
body: ## Summary - Fixes the flaky `mongo-jobs:test:ci` failure: `Background Jobs Worker › with change stream the job will be consumed right after being enqueued even if it's during the wait for new job period` - The root cause was a **race condition**: `waitForJobRunCount` resolves as soon as a `JobRun` document is created (inside `handler.perform()`), but `markJobCompleted` (which deletes the job from `backgroundJobs.jobModel`) runs *after* `perform()` returns — both are sequential awaits in `performJob()` but the test assertion fired between them. On slow/loaded CI (cache-miss Renovate runs), this window was wide enough to cause `countDocuments()` to return `1` instead of `0`. - Fix: replaced the immediate `expect(await backgroundJobs.jobModel.countDocuments()).toBe(0)` assertions with `waitForJobCount({ expectedCount: 0, ... })` calls, which poll until the job is actually deleted — consistent with the pattern used in other tests in the same file (e.g. `delivers empty nested objects to the handler perform method`). ## Root Cause In [`worker.ts:296-297`](https://github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils/blob/main/packages/mongo-jobs/src/lib/internal/worker.ts#L296-L297): ```ts await this.runJobHandler(job); // ← JobRun created here (waitForJobRunCount resolves) await this.markJobCompleted(job); // ← job deleted here (may not have run yet) ``` The test was asserting `countDocuments() === 0` immediately after `waitForJobRunCount` resolved, before `markJobCompleted` had a chance to execute. Closes insight: `mongo-jobs:test:ci flaky — persists after 15s timeout increase` --- > [!NOTE] > Created by [Mendral](https://mendral.com). Tag @mendral-app with feedback or questions. > > - [View implementation session](https://app.mendral.com/sessions/action:01KKYYC293PQYXQFH71AERYMV5) > - Addresses [this insight](https://app.mendral.com/insights/01KKH9SA77YQCNW23JNR2Z4XGM) ---

author: lucasrudi
body:
## Root cause

The `docker` profile loads only `application.yml` + `application-docker.yml`. Neither had a `messaging` section, so `telegram.webhook-secret` defaulted to `""` and `TelegramWebhookController.validateConfig()` threw on startup:

> mindtrack.messaging.telegram.webhook-secret must not be blank

The `local` profile wasn't affected because `application-local.yml` already had the messaging config.

## Changes

- Added `mindtrack.messaging.telegram` and `mindtrack.messaging.whatsapp` sections to `application-docker.yml`
- `webhook-secret` reads from `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` env var, with a local-dev default so Docker Compose works out of the box
- `whatsapp.enabled: false` matches the local profile (WhatsApp not yet configured)
- Added `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to `docker/.env.example`

Closes #242

author: alvinttang
body:
## Description

Fixes #35990.

`json.loads()` can successfully parse JSON that deserializes to non-dict types (strings, lists, integers, booleans). When this happens for tool call arguments in the Responses API path, the non-dict value is assigned to `ToolCall.args` which requires a `dict[str, Any]`, causing a `ValidationError` on `AIMessage` construction.

This PR adds an `isinstance(args, dict)` check after `json.loads()`. Non-dict results now raise a `TypeError` that is caught alongside `JSONDecodeError`, routing the malformed tool call to `invalid_tool_calls` instead of crashing.

### Changes

- **`libs/partners/openai/langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py`**: Added `isinstance(args, dict)` check after `json.loads()` in `_construct_lc_result_from_responses_api()`. Changed `except JSONDecodeError` to `except (JSONDecodeError, TypeError)`.
- **`libs/partners/openai/tests/unit_tests/chat_models/test_base.py`**: Added parameterized test covering string, list, integer, and boolean JSON arguments — all verified to route to `invalid_tool_calls`.

body:
This PR adds a new template to configure an account to run E2E tests in GitHub hooks: `tf-aws-iam-ci`.

This template scaffolds the following:
- oidc provider for GitHub (one per AWS account)
- iam roles w/ trust policy for the oidc provider
- aws secrets for:
    - 5 github oauth apps client secrets
    - bot account password & recovery code
    - `.auth` webbrowser state for 2FA access
- aws ssm parameters for the oauth app client IDs

### Maintainer experience
- run in an account: `mkdir ci-infra && cd ci-infra`
- run `init . -E terraform -P aws -I iam -T ci`, then `jd config` & `jd up`
- thereafter the project is saved in the account S3 store (bucket automatically created if not present)
- run e2e tests for ci template: `just test-e2e-ci <project-dir> <test-selector> <options>`

### Next steps
- create an AWS account for the CI
- create a GitHub account for testing bot
- create GitHub oauth apps for the bot
- configure the `ci` template, persist in the store
- run the `auth-setup` once in this account, persist in the `auth` secret
- then update the github hooks to pull the project from the store, retrieve the oauth apps client ID / client secret, keep persisting the webbrowser state in the `auth` secret
- thanks to GitHub cookie renewal, the 2FA should never kick in (provided we run the CI frequently enough, at least every 30 days)

### Implementation
- created new template directory under `./libs`
- template scaffolding w/ `manifest.yaml` and `variables.yaml`
- engine scaffolding w/ `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`
- modules for `iam_role`, `secrets` and `ssm_parameter`
- update `justfile` methods

### Testing
- add UTs
- add E2E configuration tests
- deployed from scratch, verified resource creation & secret seeds
- deployed second copy, verified no resource conflicts (ie allow n copies in an AWS account)

- Make the player-facing campaign → local → return loop clearer by making the home node (Greybridge) unmistakable on the campaign map and by surfacing immediate, bounded feedback for reward gain/turn-in and local combat outcomes.
- Address four loop-clarity problems (home visibility/usability, proof→turn-in→ration feedback, attack/readability, and honest UI about town entry) without expanding runtime profile scope or adding a second combat seam.
- Keep all authoritative invariants intact: deterministic simulation, command/event-only mutation, campaign/local role separation, and no town interior affordance in this pass.

### Description
- Viewer/UI: added high-priority home-site marker treatment and persistent label (`GREYBRIDGE HOME`) plus an in-context HUD/inspector home-node line that states supported services and that town interior is not implemented. (changes in `src/hexcrawler/cli/pygame_viewer.py`).
- Reward feedback: added bounded, event-driven HUD/inspector feedback lines for local reward grants (`Proof Token +N`) and post-turn-in ration gains (`Rations +N`), and preserved inventory counts and turn-in availability visibility.
- Combat/readability foundations: kept `attack_intent` authoritative flow but added last-combat outcome readouts (`HIT`/`MISS`, reason, neutralized=yes/no) and visually differentiated active vs incapacitated hostiles in the viewer so neutralization is legible in local playspace.
- Small tuning & honesty surface: added home-site context menu entries that explicitly list supported actions (recover, turn-in, town interior not implemented) and a small local-hostile cadence constant tweak to keep contact attack behavior readable (no second combat path introduced).
- Documentation: updated `docs/STATUS.md` to record phase/next-action and summarize what changed in this commit; added targeted tests in `tests/test_pygame_viewer_cli.py` to lock expectations.

### Testing
- Static checks: `python -m py_compile` for the modified viewer, module and new tests succeeded.
- Targeted tests run: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests/test_pygame_viewer_cli.py tests/test_reward_turn_in_loop_p5.py tests/test_local_hostile_behavior_slice.py tests/test_runtime_profiles.py` and all targeted tests passed after the small local-hostile cadence alignment fix.
- Full suite: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q` was executed; result: 726 passed, 1 warning.
- Note: failing test encountered during iteration was fixed by restoring the intended `LOCAL_CONTACT_ATTACK_COOLDOWN_TICKS` behavior; all automated tests green after the fix.

body:
## Summary

Replace env var-based versioning with a `__version__` file as the single source of truth. This ensures all deployment methods (staging via Cloud Run, releases via GitHub Actions) get consistent versioning without needing to pass build args.

## Changes

- Add `__version__` file containing semantic version (currently 0.0.11)
- Update `config.py` to read version from `__version__` file (falls back to "dev" if missing)
- Remove `APP_VERSION` ARG/ENV from both Dockerfiles
- Update release workflow to write version to `__version__`, commit with `[skip ci]`, and push before tagging
- Update release workflow docker job to checkout `main` (ensures it picks up the version bump commit)

## Why

Staging deployment was showing `version: "dev"` because Cloud Run's direct Dockerfile build doesn't pass the `APP_VERSION` build arg. Using a source-controlled `__version__` file ensures every deployment method gets the correct version automatically.

## Summary

- **Configurable screenshot capture** via environment variables so users can opt into full-resolution output for human review while keeping Anthropic vision-optimized defaults:
  - `SCREENSHOT_MAX_WIDTH` — default `1568` (Anthropic vision optimal), set to `0` to uncap
  - `SCREENSHOT_MAX_HEIGHT` — default `8000`, set to `0` to uncap  
  - `SCREENSHOT_FORMAT` — default `jpeg` for viewport/fullpage, `png` for element crops. Override to `png` for lossless everywhere
  - `SCREENSHOT_QUALITY` — default `80`, range 1-100 for JPEG quality
- **Fixed integration test viewport/scale mismatch** — test context was `1280×720, deviceScaleFactor: 1` but production uses `1280×800, deviceScaleFactor: 2`. Tests now match production settings.
- **Fixed pre-existing unit test bug** — `constrainScreenshot` height-limit test asserted `height <= 1568` but `MAX_SCREENSHOT_HEIGHT` has always been `8000`. Updated test image from 2000px to 9000px tall and corrected assertions to match the actual cap.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `capture.ts` | Added `parseScreenshotDimension()`, `getScreenshotFormatOverride()`, `getScreenshotQualityDefault()` helpers; dimension constants now read from env vars |
| `tools/screenshot.ts` | Screenshot tool respects format/quality env var overrides for both viewport and element screenshots |
| `tests/browser-tools-integration.test.mjs` | Fixed viewport to `1280×800` and added `deviceScaleFactor: 2` to match production |
| `tests/browser-tools-unit.test.cjs` | Fixed height-limit test: image 1000×9000, assertions use 8000 cap |

## Usage

Default behavior is unchanged. For full-resolution screenshots:

```bash
SCREENSHOT_MAX_WIDTH=0 SCREENSHOT_MAX_HEIGHT=0 SCREENSHOT_FORMAT=png SCREENSHOT_QUALITY=100
```

author: gutslabs
body:
## What does this PR do?
Fixes a parallel tool execution safety bug in the agent run loop.

Previously, path-scoped file operations were compared using raw lexical paths. That meant two tool calls targeting the same file through different path spellings (for example `notes.txt` and `subdir/../notes.txt`) could be misclassified as independent and executed in parallel.

This change normalizes path-scoped tool targets before overlap checks so same-target file operations fall back to sequential execution.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Safety fix
- [x] Tests

## Changes Made
- Normalize path-scoped file operation targets before overlap detection
- Prevent same-file alias paths from being treated as independent
- Added regression tests for normalized overlap detection

## How to Test
1. Run `source .venv/bin/activate`
2. Run `pytest tests/test_run_agent.py -q -k 'ParallelScopeNormalization or TestPathsOverlap'`
3. Confirm `notes.txt` and `subdir/../notes.txt` are treated as overlapping
4. Confirm the batch falls back to sequential execution

- provide a benchmark surface to distinguish "planner cannot solve anything" from "planner fails on the paper matrix"

## Why
Three planners currently show zero success on the paper matrix. That is suspicious, but it does not tell us whether they are fundamentally broken or just outside the useful operating regime of the benchmark scenarios. This PR adds a minimal sanity benchmark to answer that question quickly.

## Validation
- `uv run python scripts/validation/svg_inspect.py maps/svg_maps/planner_sanity_open.svg --show-routes`
- `uv run python scripts/tools/run_camera_ready_benchmark.py --config configs/benchmarks/planner_sanity_matrix_v1.yaml --label planner_sanity_open_space --log-level INFO`
- `uv run python scripts/tools/analyze_camera_ready_campaign.py --campaign-root output/benchmarks/camera_ready/planner_sanity_matrix_v1_planner_sanity_open_space_20260318_151135`

## Result
On the trivial open-space sanity scenario:
- `orca`, `ppo`, `prediction_planner`, and `socnav_sampling` each reached `1.0` success over 3/3 seeds
- `goal`, `social_force`, and `sacadrl` remained at `0.0` success and timed out at `max_steps`

That means the paper-matrix zero-success results are not a universal benchmark artifact. We now have a compact regression surface for debugging the remaining three planners.

- **`scripts/Create-CpmLegacyTestSolution.ps1`** — Generates a minimal test solution (legacy non-SDK `.csproj` + `Directory.Packages.props` with CPM enabled) for manually verifying the CPM fix without needing an existing project.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

This PR addresses [NuGet/Home#9521](https://github.com/NuGet/Home/issues/9521): **Central Package Management (CPM) is not supported in the Visual Studio Package Manager UI for legacy (non-SDK-style) projects**.

### Current Behavior

When a solution has CPM enabled (`Directory.Packages.props` with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>`) and contains **legacy (non-SDK-style)** `.csproj` projects:

1. Installing or updating a package via the VS Package Manager UI **adds `<Version>` tags directly to the `.csproj` file** instead of updating `Directory.Packages.props`.
2. In **mixed solutions** (SDK + legacy projects): both `Directory.Packages.props` and the `.csproj` get modified — polluting and breaking CPM.

### Root Cause

In `LegacyPackageReferenceProject.InstallPackageAsync`, the version range is always passed as part of the `LibraryDependency`, which then flows through `VsManagedLanguagesProjectSystemServices.AddOrUpdatePackageReferenceAsync` → `_vsProject4.PackageReferences.AddOrUpdate(name, version, ...)` — this always writes the version into the `.csproj` via the VS DTE API, ignoring CPM entirely.

The `GetPackageSpecAsync` method already detects CPM (`isCpvmEnabled`) and reads central versions correctly for restore — but `InstallPackageAsync` has no CPM awareness.

---

## Required Changes

### 1. `src/NuGet.Clients/NuGet.PackageManagement.VisualStudio/Projects/LegacyPackageReferenceProject.cs`

Modify `InstallPackageAsync` to detect whether CPM is enabled for the project. If CPM is enabled:
- Add the `<PackageReference>` to the `.csproj` **without a version** (pass `null` as `versionRange` in the `LibraryRange`).
- Add or update the `<PackageVersion>` entry in `Directory.Packages.props` using direct XML file manipulation (load the props file from the solution directory, add/update the `PackageVersion` item, save).

If CPM is **not** enabled, keep the existing behavior (pass version in `LibraryDependency` as today).

**Steps:**
1. After the argument validation, read the `ManagePackageVersionsCentrally` MSBuild property using `_vsProjectAdapter.BuildProperties` (same pattern as in `GetPackageSpecAsync`).
2. If CPM is enabled:
   a. Create the `LibraryDependency` with `versionRange: null` (no version in the `.csproj`).
   b. Call `ProjectServices.References.AddOrUpdatePackageReferenceAsync(dependency, token)` — this adds `<PackageReference Include="Foo" />` without a version.
   c. Find `Directory.Packages.props` by walking up from the project directory (look for the file that contains `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>`). The path can be read from the MSBuild property `DirectoryPackagesPropsPath` via `_vsProjectAdapter.BuildProperties.GetPropertyValue("DirectoryPackagesPropsPath")`.
   d. Load the XML file, find or create an `<ItemGroup>` with `<PackageVersion Include="packageId" Version="..."/>`, set/update the `Version` attribute, and save.
   e. Ensure this is done on the UI thread (`await _threadingService.JoinableTaskFactory.SwitchToMainThreadAsync()`) as needed, but the XML file I/O should be done off the UI thread.
3. If CPM is **not** enabled: keep existing behavior exactly as today.

**Detection of `DirectoryPackagesPropsPath`:**
```csharp
string directoryPackagesPropsPath = _vsProjectAdapter.BuildProperties.GetPropertyValue("DirectoryPackagesPropsPath");
```

**Detection of CPM:**
```csharp
#pragma warning disable CS0618
bool isCpvmEnabled = MSBuildStringUtility.IsTrue(GetPropertySafe(_vsProjectAdapter.BuildProperties, ProjectBuildProperties.ManagePackageVersionsCentrally));
#pragma warning restore CS0618
```

**XML update pattern** (update or add `<PackageVersion>` in `Directory.Packages.props`):
```csharp
// Load XML
var doc = XDocument.Load(directoryPackagesPropsPath);
var ns = doc.Root?.Name.Namespace ?? XNamespace.None;

// Find existing PackageVersion element for this package
var existingItem = doc.Descendants(ns + "PackageVersion")
    .FirstOrDefault(e => string.Equals(e.Attribute("Include")?.Value, packageId, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

string versionString = range.OriginalString ?? range.MinVersion.ToNormalizedString();

if (existingItem != null)
{
    existingItem.SetAttributeValue("Version", versionString);
}
else
{
    // Find or create ItemGroup
    var itemGroup = doc.Root?.Elements(ns + "ItemGroup").LastOrDefault()
        ?? new XElement(ns + "ItemGroup");
    if (!doc.Root.Elements(ns + "ItemGroup").Any())
    {
        doc.Root.Add(itemGroup);
    }
    itemGroup.Add(new XElement(ns + "PackageVersion",
        new XAttribute("Include", packageId),
        new XAttribute("Version", versionString)));
}
doc.Save(directoryPackagesPropsPath);
```

### 2. `src/NuGet.Clients/NuGet.PackageManagement.VisualStudio/ProjectServices/VsManagedLanguagesProjectSystemServices.cs`

The `AddOrUpdatePackageReferenceAsync` method calls `_vsProject4.PackageReferences.AddOrUpdate(name, version, ...)`. W...

author: kimimgo
body:
closes #55969

## Summary

When using `df.loc[(np.datetime64(...), 'A')]` on a MultiIndex whose first level
contains `datetime.date` objects, the second-level key (`'A'`) was silently ignored,
returning all rows matching the date instead of filtering by subsequent levels.

## Root Cause

In `MultiIndex._partial_tup_index`, the containment check `lab not in lev` uses
hash-based lookup. `np.datetime64` and `datetime.date` have different hashes despite
comparing equal, so `np.datetime64('2023-11-01') not in Index([datetime.date(2023, 11, 1)])`
returns `True`. This triggers the short-circuit path that skips all subsequent level filtering.

## Fix

Convert `np.datetime64` keys to Python datetime objects via `.item()` before the
containment check, so the hash-based lookup matches correctly.

author: openhouse
body:
### Motivation
- The previous code blindly sliced a large `project-overview.txt` by characters and injected the entire (or truncated) text into every meeting, causing biased context, Node OOMs, and TPM/rate-limit failures.
- The intent is to separate archival dumps from model-facing context, budget by tokens not chars, and pace requests by tokens-per-minute / requests-per-minute rather than worker count alone.
- Meeting prompts must be rearranged so the large shared prefix is stable across meetings and per-meeting bits come last to enable prompt caching.
- The run must be resilient to 429s/timeouts via retries/backoff and must fail fast when preflight shows the request would exceed configured token caps.

### Description
- Replaced blind char truncation with token-budgeted overview fitting via `src/contextBudget.js` and `fitOverviewToTokenBudget`, which parses a directory section plus `### File:` blocks and prioritizes sections by recency, prompt/path relevance, and file-importance heuristics (with a balanced fallback); it always includes the directory/manifest summary and an omission note.
- Added a lightweight project manifest builder `src/manifest.js` and now write `project-manifest.jsonl` for grounding so the model can reference exact relative paths even when content summaries are bounded.
- Introduced token-aware CLI/config knobs and validation in `src/config.js` (`--max-input-tokens`, `--max-overview-tokens`, `--reserve-output-tokens` / `--max-output-tokens`, `--tpm-limit`, `--max-requests-per-minute`, `--request-timeout-ms`, `--max-retries`, `--dry-run`) and normalized GPT-5 reasoning-effort handling.
- Implemented a rolling-window scheduler and backoff utilities in `src/rateLimiter.js` and a token-aware preflight + dispatcher in `bin/packet-select.js` that computes safe worker counts from TPM/RPM budgets and writes `preflight.txt` and other debug artifacts.
- Migrated meeting execution to the Responses API in `src/meeting.js` with structured JSON-schema output, explicit `max_output_tokens`, retries with exponential backoff + jitter, `prompt_cache_key` support, and request usage/IDs captured in meeting metadata.
- Created model-facing artifacts: `project-overview.llm.txt`, `project-manifest.jsonl`, `context-selected.txt`, `context-stats.json`, and `preflight.txt` (written under `--out-dir`).
- Upgraded `openai` dependency to `^6.32.0` in `package.json` to access Responses and token-counting surfaces and adjusted the wrapper script to use `PACKET_SELECT_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` for optional Node heap tuning.
- Reordered prompt construction so shared static content (instructions, schema, manifest, fitted overview) appears before per-meeting curator names/round info to improve prefix cacheability.

### Testing
- Ran the unit test suite with `npm test` (includes new tests for overview fitting, rolling-window scheduler, and prompt ordering), and all tests passed (new tests exercised `fitOverviewToTokenBudget`, `RollingWindowScheduler`, and `buildMeetingInput`).
- Performed a dry-run smoke check: `node ./bin/packet-select.js --src-root <tmp> --prompt 'Pick files' --curators 'A,B' --sample-size 1 --api-key dummy --out-dir <tmp/out> --dry-run --verbose` which generated `preflight.txt`, `project-manifest.jsonl`, `project-overview.llm.txt`, and exited before API calls successfully.
- Added small integration/observability: preflight reports estimated input tokens and warns when exact token counting falls back to heuristics; retry/backoff behavior exercised by unit tests for backoff timing logic.

------

author: skybristol
body:
## Summary

Fixes silent validation failures in `validate_value_from_list` that caused every real-world value list check to return `valid=False` regardless of whether the value was actually present in the cache.

## Root Causes Fixed

**Bug 1 - Wrong cache format**: The old implementation read `cache_data["results"]["bindings"]` (raw SPARQL wire format), but every SpiritSafe materialized cache artifact uses `cache_data["items"]` list format. No real value ever matched.

**Bug 2 - Wrong value normalization**: The old implementation compared values as stripped QIDs (e.g. `"Q12345"`), but the wizard stores full Wikidata entity URIs (e.g. `"http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q12345"`). Even if the format bug were fixed, values would never match.

## Changes

### `gkc/fermenter.py`

- `_normalize_item_to_uri()` - Converts all incoming value shapes to a canonical full Wikidata URI:
  - Full URI string - returned as-is
  - `"Q12345"` string - expanded to `"http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q12345"`
  - `{"item": uri, ...}` dict (wizard format) - recurse on `uri`
  - `{"id": qid, ...}` dict (Wikibase snakvalue format) - recurse on `qid`
  - Anything else - `None` (unnormalizable, fails validation)

- `_extract_cache_uris_and_labels()` - Reads both cache formats:
  - SpiritSafe `"items"` list: `entry["item"]` URI, `entry["itemLabel"]` plain string label
  - Raw SPARQL `"results.bindings"`: `binding["item"]["value"]` URI, `binding["itemLabel"]["value"]` label

- `validate_value_from_list()` - Updated to use the two helpers above; short-circuits empty/None as valid (presence enforcement is upstream in `validate_entity_packet_data`).

### `tests/test_fermenter_value_list.py`

19 tests covering:
- `items` format: full URI hit/miss, QID string hit/miss, wizard dict hit/miss, Wikibase snakvalue dict hit
- `items` format fuzzy: label hit/miss
- SPARQL bindings format: strict hit/miss, fuzzy hit
- Edge cases: cache missing, corrupt JSON, None/empty/empty-dict input, unnormalizable value, both formats present in one file

## Related

Closes the pre-flight blocker identified in issue #144 Phase D comments. Phase D wizard UI work (type-ahead filtering on `wikibase-item` inputs in `StatementsStep`) can proceed after this merges.

Float32 support requires (1) that the Domain is Float32, and (2) that the backend supports it. Backends that support Float32 are `Backend.Quadrature` (provided the nodes and weights are converted to Float32), QuadGK and HCubature, but not Cubature (hence the @broken_test in this PR)

```julia
julia> nodes, weights = gausslegendre(50);

julia> J = integral(cos, Domain.Box1D(-Float32(π/2),Float32(π/2)); backend = Backend.Quadrature(Float32.(nodes), Float32.(weights)));

julia> J()
1.9999998f0
```

body:
1. **Suppress startup warning**: "Starting a Matplotlib GUI outside of the main thread will likely fail" — this is a false positive since WebAgg only uses software (Agg) rendering and communicates over the network, no GUI toolkit is involved.

2. **Reduce log noise**: Downgrade "Received message for unknown comm" from WARNING to DEBUG — this is an expected race condition when comms are closed during cell re-execution or server shutdown.

3. **Fix shutdown crash**: Properly clean up the figure manager (remove web socket, close canvas) when a cell is re-run or deleted, preventing dangling timer callbacks that cause "QObject::killTimer: Timers cannot be stopped from another thread" errors and segfaults.

author: simonshah7
body:
## Summary
This PR decouples drag interaction and layout computation from the monolithic `TimelineView` component by extracting them into reusable hooks (`useTimelineDrag`, `useActivityLayout`) and a presentational component (`ActivityBar`). This improves testability, performance, and maintainability of the timeline's core interaction logic.

## Key Changes

### Component Refactoring
- **Extract `useActivityLayout` hook**: Computes vertical stacking layout for activities within swimlanes. Memoized to only recompute when activities, swimlanes, or row height change—not on every mouse move during drag.
- **Extract `useTimelineDrag` hook**: Encapsulates all drag, resize, and move state and handlers. Manages temporary activity state during interactions and handles rollback on failed API calls.
- **Extract `ActivityBar` component**: Presentational component for rendering individual activity bars with resize handles and action buttons (clone, edit).
- **Extract `TimelineHeader` component**: Renders the timeline header with date labels and day columns, supporting year/quarter/month zoom levels.
- **Create `components/timeline/index.ts`**: Barrel export for timeline subcomponents and hooks.

### State Management Improvements
- Separate "base layout" (from `useActivityLayout`) from "display layout" (base + drag overlay). Display layout only recomputes affected swimlanes during drag, reducing unnecessary recalculation.
- Move drag state (`isDragging`, `dragStart`, `dragCurrent`, `resizing`, `moving`, `tempActivity`) into `useTimelineDrag` hook.
- Store pre-drag state in `useTimelineDrag` for rollback on failed API calls.

### API & Data Fixes
- **Fix currency enum**: Change from display symbols (`'US$'`, `'UK£'`) to ISO codes (`'USD'`, `'GBP'`, `'EUR'`) in schema and throughout codebase.
- **Add batch activity creation endpoint** (`/api/activities/batch`): Allows creating multiple activities in a single request with validation.
- **Add swimlane reorder endpoint** (`/api/swimlanes/reorder`): Batch update sort order instead of individual requests.
- **Define JSONB shapes**: Add TypeScript interfaces for `ActivityDependency` and `ActivityAttachment` in schema.

### Export & Utility Improvements
- **Extract export logic** to `lib/export.ts`: Move PNG and CSV export functions out of `app/page.tsx`.
- **Update `app/page.tsx`**: Use batch endpoints, fix currency defaults to `'USD'`, improve error handling in `handleActivityUpdate`.
- **Update seed data**: Use ISO currency codes.

### Performance & Code Quality
- Remove unused `framer-motion` import from `TimelineView` (animation logic moved to extracted components).
- Improve swimlane reorder to use single batch API call instead of Promise.all of individual requests.
- Add proper error handling and validation in batch endpoints.

## Notable Implementation Details
- The display layout computation in `TimelineView` now intelligently recomputes only affected swimlanes during drag, avoiding full recalculation on every mouse move.
- `useTimelineDrag` provides a clean interface: `dragState`, `tempActivity`, and four handler functions (`handleEmptyMouseDown`, `handleActivityMouseDown`, `handleMouseMove`, `handleMouseUp`).
- Currency and region validation extracted to utility functions in API routes for reuse.
