## Summary
- **Kafka consumer** (`CatalogSyncConsumer`) listens to `stoa.api.lifecycle` events (`api-created`, `api-updated`, `api-deleted`) and triggers a targeted single-API sync into `api_catalog`
- **Periodic worker** (`CatalogSyncWorker`) runs a full catalog sync every 5 min (configurable via `CATALOG_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS`) + initial sync on startup — safety net for missed Kafka events
- **Bug fix**: `/catalog-entries` endpoint now filters `deleted_at IS NULL` to exclude soft-deleted APIs
- New `sync_single_api()` method on `CatalogSyncService` for lightweight per-API sync

## Context
The gateway-deployments dropdown and portal API catalog were empty because `api_catalog` (PostgreSQL cache) was only populated via manual `POST /v1/admin/catalog/sync`. APIs created through the UI go to GitLab but the cache was never auto-updated.

## Files changed
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `consumers/catalog_sync_consumer.py` | **New** — Kafka consumer for API lifecycle events |
| `workers/catalog_sync_worker.py` | **New** — Periodic full sync worker |
| `services/catalog_sync_service.py` | Add `sync_single_api()` method |
| `routers/gateway_deployments.py` | Add `deleted_at IS NULL` filter |
| `main.py` | Wire consumer + worker in lifespan |

body:
## Summary
This change enhances the babysitter's feedback follow-up mechanism by extracting structured summaries from the agent's output and including them in GitHub follow-up comments. Instead of just posting the audit token, follow-up comments now include a concise summary of what the agent did or why it was blocked.

## Key Changes
- **Updated agent prompt**: Modified the instructions to ask the agent to emit structured `FEEDBACK_SUMMARY_START`/`FEEDBACK_SUMMARY_END` blocks with audit tokens and concise summaries for each feedback item addressed or blocked on
- **Added summary extraction**: Implemented `extractAgentSummaries()` function that parses the agent output using regex to extract audit tokens and their corresponding summaries into a Map
- **Enhanced follow-up comments**: Updated `buildFeedbackFollowUpBody()` to accept an optional `agentSummary` parameter and include it in the follow-up comment body between the headline and audit token
- **Integrated extraction into workflow**: Added a call to `extractAgentSummaries()` after successful agent execution to populate the summaries map, which is then passed when building follow-up comments
- **Updated tests**: Modified test to verify the new structured output format and confirm that agent summaries are correctly extracted and included in follow-up comments

## Implementation Details
- The regex pattern `FEEDBACK_SUMMARY_BLOCK` captures audit tokens in the format `codefactory-feedback:*` and extracts the summary text between the markers
- Summaries are stored in a Map keyed by audit token for efficient lookup when building follow-ups
- The extraction happens after agent completion but before follow-up comments are posted, ensuring all summaries are available
- Logging includes the count of extracted summaries for observability

# What does this PR do?

Implements the full Shipper Dashboard frontend for LoadLink Rwanda. This includes all pages a shipper needs to manage their shipments from posting to rating layout, navigation, forms, and API connections.

- `Loads` — lists all shipper shipments with status chips for all 7 statuses (POSTED, AWAITING_ESCROW, ESCROW_FUNDED, IN_TRANSIT, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, COMPLETED, DISPUTED). Click to expand details. Shows action buttons based on status
- `PostShipment` — form with all Rwanda districts dropdown, cargo description, weight, price, date picker. Validates all fields before submit
- `InterestedTrucks` — lists trucks that expressed interest in a shipment, sorted by rating. Confirm modal before selecting a truck

- `DeliveryConfirmation` — real-time 24hr countdown timer, Confirm Delivery and Report Issue buttons
- `RateTruck` — 5-star interactive selector, optional comment, submits rating after completion

1. Clone the branch `feature/frontend-shipper-dashboard`
2. Run `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev`

body:
## Summary

This PR prepares the first conservative backup management scope on `feature/backup`.

Included:
- non-blocking backup size estimation with progress/state
- manual backup target configuration and validation
- manual files-only backup execution for local and safe-subset ssh/rsync targets
- structured backup reporting and conservative verification/readiness signaling
- UI integration for target management, size visibility, validation, execution states, and warnings
- documentation and terminology hardening
- minimal FastAPI lifespan migration for background-job shutdown

## Safety boundaries

This PR intentionally does not claim full backup or disaster-recovery readiness.

Current limits:
- manual execution is files-only
- SMB is configuration/validation/mount-planning only
- restore execution is not implemented
- verification is conservative and does not provide strong end-to-end integrity guarantees
- parallel rsync is documented as future design work, not enabled by default

## Risks / follow-up

- `completed` means execution completed for the implemented scope only
- target validation covers only currently implemented checks
- snapshot visibility does not imply a full restore point
- branch currently also contains a preserved `LICENSE` update unrelated to backup behavior

`pnpm build:compile:esm:packages` will do a minimal ESM only package build.

Can be used to check validity of production code without hitting test collateral (except for a few test-oriented packages).

`build:esnext` tasks (`fluid-build --task build:esnext`) are able to complete without needing to build CommonJS with these changes:

body:
### Motivation
- The Quant UI could crash with `Unexpected token '<'` when starting a backtest because the frontend attempted to `response.json()` on an HTML page (Vite dev server index) instead of the API response.
- Local dev had no proxy for `/api` and `/socket.io`, so some requests hit the frontend dev server rather than the Node backend.
- The backtest start endpoint did not consistently return structured JSON on synchronous errors, which made debugging the failure harder.

### Description
- Add a Vite dev-server proxy and ESM-safe `__dirname` resolution in `client/vite.config.js` so `/api` and `/socket.io` requests route to `http://localhost:3000` during development.
- Harden the client request helper in `client/src/services/quantApi.js` to check `Content-Type` before parsing and throw a clear error when a non-JSON response (e.g. HTML) is returned.
- Wrap the server backtest start handler in `try/catch` in `server/index.js` so synchronous failures produce structured JSON errors instead of an HTML error page.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` successfully to build the client assets.
- Verified server static config and JS syntax with `node --check server/index.js` which passed.
- Verified ESM config for Vite with `node --input-type=module -e "import('./client/vite.config.js')"` which printed success.
- Exercised the backtest API with a `curl -X POST` to `http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/quant/backtests` and received a valid JSON job response (success).

author: raphaelmanke
body:
## Problem

When the Kiro server returns `invalid_grant` / `Invalid grant provided` during token refresh, the error was not recognized as a fatal auth failure. This caused the plugin to:
- Re-throw the error instead of marking the account unhealthy
- Retry the dead token up to 10 times before giving up
- Silently swallow `writeToKiroCli` failures, causing stale tokens to persist

## Changes

- Add `Invalid grant provided` and `invalid_grant` to `isPermanentError()` so accounts fail fast
- Catch `Invalid grant provided` in `token-refresher` error handler
- Fix CLI sync skip condition to also verify token is not already expired (`expires_at > Date.now()`)
- Log `writeToKiroCli` failures instead of silently swallowing them

## Root cause

`invalid_grant` is returned when a refresh token is revoked, expired server-side, or invalidated by a concurrent refresh (rotation race). The fix ensures these are treated as permanent failures requiring re-authentication rather than transient errors worth retrying.

Related to #43 #49

## Fix grader, task, setup, and solution to ensure agents can score > 0

The evaluation has been scoring 0/1.0 across all 10 runs. After deep analysis of the full file set (`grader.py`, `task.yaml`, `setup.sh`, `solution.sh`), here are all the root-cause bugs and required fixes:

---

### Fix 1 — `grader.py` `check_1_init_guard_present`: Strengthen the guard check

**Problem:** Currently only checks `"-s /config/queues.conf" in script`. An agent can satisfy this with a comment line or partial patch. It also doesn't verify the second file guard.

**Fix:** Require ALL of the following to be present in the script:
- `-s /config/queues.conf`
- `-s /config/exchanges.conf`
- `sleep 2`

```python
def check_1_init_guard_present() -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Does validate-config.sh contain the -s guard for BOTH files?"""
    rc, script = run_kubectl([
        "-n", NAMESPACE, "get", "configmap", "fanout-init-script",
        "-o", "jsonpath={.data.validate-config\\.sh}"
    ])
    if rc != 0 or not script:
        return False, "fanout-init-script ConfigMap not found"
    has_queue_guard = "-s /config/queues.conf" in script
    has_exchange_guard = "-s /config/exchanges.conf" in script
    has_retry = "sleep 2" in script
    if has_queue_guard and has_exchange_guard and has_retry:
        return True, "guard present"
    missing = []
    if not has_queue_guard:
        missing.append("-s /config/queues.conf")
    if not has_exchange_guard:
        missing.append("-s /config/exchanges.conf")
    if not has_retry:
        missing.append("sleep 2")
    return False, f"guard missing: {', '.join(missing)}"
```

---

### Fix 2 — `grader.py` `check_2_init_exit_zero`: Skip own rollout if pod already healthy + increase timeout

**Problem:** The grader always triggers a new rollout restart even if the agent already did a successful one. This adds unnecessary latency, can interfere with a freshly-completed agent rollout, and the 120s timeout is too short for k3s under load.

**Fix:**
- Check if the newest pod's init container already has exit code `0` and logs contain no ERROR. If so, skip the grader's own rollout restart.
- Increase rollout timeout from 120s to 180s.
- Store the successfully-checked pod name in a module-level variable `_LATEST_POD` for `check_3` to reuse.

```python
_LATEST_POD = ""

def check_2_init_exit_zero() -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """After rolling restart, init container exits 0 and no ERROR in logs."""
    global _LATEST_POD

    # Check if pod is already healthy (agent already did the rollout)
    pod = get_newest_pod()
    already_healthy = False
    if pod:
        rc_ec, exit_code = run_kubectl([
            "-n", NAMESPACE, "get", "pod", pod,
            "-o", "jsonpath={.status.initContainerStatuses[0].state.terminated.exitCode}"
        ])
        rc_logs, logs = run_kubectl(["-n", NAMESPACE, "logs", pod, "-c", "config-validator"])
        if rc_ec == 0 and exit_code == "0" and "ERROR: config files still empty" not in logs:
            already_healthy = True

    if not already_healthy:
        # Trigger rolling restart
        rc, _ = run_kubectl(["-n", NAMESPACE, "rollout", "restart", "deployment/fanout-service"])
        if rc != 0:
            return False, "rollout restart failed"

        # Wait for rollout to complete (180s)
        rc, _ = run_kubectl(
            ["-n", NAMESPACE, "rollout", "status", "deployment/fanout-service", "--timeout=180s"],
            timeout=190
        )
        if rc != 0:
            return False, "rollout did not complete"

    pod = get_newest_pod()
    if not pod:
        return False, "no pod found"

    # Wait for init container to reach terminated state
    for _ in range(30):
        rc_ec, exit_code = run_kubectl([
            "-n", NAMESPACE, "get", "pod", pod,
            "-o", "jsonpath={.status.initContainerStatuses[0].state.terminated.exitCode}"
        ])
        if rc_ec == 0 and exit_code != "":
            break
        import time; time.sleep(2)

    if exit_code != "0":
        return False, f"init exit code: {exit_code}"

    rc_logs, logs = run_kubectl(["-n", NAMESPACE, "logs", pod, "-c", "config-validator"])
    if "ERROR: config files still empty" in logs:
        return False, "ERROR in init logs"

    _LATEST_POD = pod
    return True, "init exit 0"
```

---

### Fix 3 — `grader.py` `check_3_config_nonempty_at_init`: Use regex instead of hardcoded word + use shared pod

**Problem:** The check looks for `"queues.conf: fanout"` which hardcodes the string "fanout" — a word that only appears in the ConfigMap value if the agent restores it to the exact original value. Additionally if `check_2` ran a new rollout, `check_3` must use the same new pod — not a stale one.

## Summary
This change enhances the Kalshi market normalization to automatically generate a complementary NO outcome for true binary markets (single market with one outcome), providing a complete two-sided view of the market.

## Key Changes
- Added logic to detect single-market binary outcomes in Kalshi events
- Automatically generate a NO outcome when a YES outcome exists as the only outcome
- Calculate NO bid/ask prices as the mathematical complement of YES prices (using 1 - price formula)
- Mirror the YES outcome's metadata (percentage, color, delta, estimate flag) with appropriate inversions for the NO side

## Implementation Details
- The complementary NO outcome is only added when `markets.length === 1 && outcomes.length === 1`
- NO bid price is calculated as `max(0, 1 - yesAsk)` and NO ask as `min(1, 1 - yesBid)` to ensure valid probability bounds
- The NO outcome's percentage is inverted (`100 - yesOut.pct`) and delta is negated to reflect the opposite position
- Handles edge cases where bid/ask prices may be zero or undefined

body:
Fixes #36645

The IsolatedPhrase match mode in FilterCriteria used \s (whitespace) as word boundaries, meaning a search term had to be surrounded by spaces (or start/end of string) to match.

This caused songs with titles like
'Music Theme "Some Artist"' to not appear when searching for "Some Artist", since the phrase was bounded by quote characters rather than spaces.

This change extends the boundary pattern to also accept Unicode punctuation (\p{P}) alongside whitespace, so terms surrounded by quotes, commas are correctly matched as isolated phrases.

Tests have been added to cover searching for terms adjacent to punctuation boundaries
(TestCriteriaMatchingTermsAdjacentToPunctuation).

Tests cover the example mentioned above.

author: arnavs
body:
### Motivation
- Align the Deep CFR training loop and sampling with the algorithm’s per-iteration advantage-net training semantics. 
- Make the in-memory traversal and GameState behavior faithful to the engine’s betting/discard rules. 
- Fix incorrect opponent-action inference used by the runtime posterior updater so range updates use observed opponent actions. 

### Description
- Retrain value/advantage nets from per-iteration traversal samples instead of a cross-iteration reservoir by creating `iter_vb_bufs`/`iter_vd_bufs` and training from them each iteration. (`submission/train.py`).
- Record average-strategy samples only for the traverser and store explicit sample weights; strategy samples are now added as `reach_traverser * iteration` into `StrategyBuffer`, and `StrategyBuffer.add()` stores an explicit weight field. (`submission/traversal.py`, `submission/network.py`).
- Preserve discard decisions during all-in traversal and run remaining streets to showdown only after mandatory discards are resolved, improving parity with the engine’s discard rules. (`submission/traversal.py`).
- Make fold always legal in the `GameState` betting mask to match the engine’s semantics. (`submission/traversal.py`).
- Change runtime posterior updates to key on the match-provided `opp_last_action` (e.g. "RAISE", "CHECK", "CALL") and only apply updates once per observed opponent action; reset and track `last_opp_action` per hand. (`submission/player.py`, `match.py` integration). 
- Add regression checks validating fold legality in the local betting mask and that `StrategyBuffer` preserves explicit sample weights. (`submission/test.py`).

### Testing
- Ran the submission regression script with `python submission/test.py`, which passed all checks (bet/raise semantics, discard order, fold legality, and strategy-buffer weight test). — success.
- Compiled the submission package with `python -m compileall submission` to verify syntax, which succeeded. — success.
- Performed a one-off traversal smoke check using `PYTHONPATH=... python - <<'PY'` to confirm only the traverser’s average-strategy buffer is populated during a traverser traversal. — success.

author: hadar01
body:
## What this PR does

Adds PEP 484 type annotations and improves docstrings across 12 transpiler
analysis and utility passes:

**Analysis passes** (`qiskit/transpiler/passes/analysis/`):
`CountOps`, `Depth`, `Size`, `Width`, `NumQubits`, `NumTensorFactors`,
`CountOpsLongestPath`, `DAGLongestPath`, `ResourceEstimation`

**Utility passes** (`qiskit/transpiler/passes/utils/`):
`DAGFixedPoint`, `FixedPoint`, `ContainsInstruction`

### Specific changes
- Add `from __future__ import annotations` to all 12 files
- Type-annotate `__init__` parameters (`bool`, `str`, `set[str]`) and
  `run()` signatures (`dag: DAGCircuit`) with `-> None` return types
- Expand sparse docstrings with `Args` blocks where missing
- Fix incorrect module-level docstring in `contains_instruction.py`
  (was a copy-paste leftover: *"Check if a property reached a fixed point"*)
- Rename the placeholder parameter `_` to `dag` in
  `ResourceEstimation.run()` for clarity and consistency

## Motivation

These passes are part of the public API and used across the transpiler
pipeline, yet they lacked type annotations — hurting IDE auto-completion,
static analysis (mypy / pyright), and Sphinx-generated API documentation.
This is a low-risk, documentation-quality improvement with **zero behavioral
changes**.

## How it was tested

- **`ruff check`** — all checks passed
- **`black --check`** — 13 files left unchanged
- **AST validation script** — confirmed `from __future__ import annotations`
  and typed `run()` return annotations present in all 12 files
- Changes are purely additive type hints and docstrings; CI will validate
  the full test suite

## Summary

Adds a `publish-pypi` job to the SDK publish workflow that uses [Speakeasy's PyPI trusted publishing action](https://github.com/speakeasy-api/sdk-generation-action/tree/main/publish-pypi) to publish packages via OIDC instead of static API tokens. This eliminates stored credentials and reduces supply chain attack surface by generating short-lived, workflow-scoped tokens.

The job runs after the existing `publish` job, gated on `python_regenerated`, `publish_python`, and `use_pypi_trusted_publishing` outputs.

For more details on the security benefits and setup: https://www.speakeasy.com/blog/pypi-trusted-publishing-security#setting-up-pypi-trusted-publishing-with-speakeasy

body:
💡 What: Refactored `markMessagesProcessed` in `src/db.ts` to use a statically prepared statement with SQLite's `json_each` function, passing the array of IDs as a JSON string instead of dynamically mapping placeholders for an `IN (?, ?, ...)` clause.

🎯 Why: The original implementation compiled a new prepared statement every time the array length changed. This bypasses the performance benefits of `better-sqlite3`'s statement caching, incurs unnecessary string allocation/concatenation overhead, and pollutes the statement cache with one-off queries.

📊 Impact: Reduces query time for repeated batch updates by ~40-50% (measured from ~9ms down to ~5ms for batches of varying length over 100 iterations) and avoids potential "too many SQL variables" errors for very large batches.

🔬 Measurement: Local benchmarks demonstrate that the JSON parsing approach is significantly faster for repeated invocations with variable array lengths. Tests and type checks ensure no regressions were introduced.

### Summary
This PR introduces comprehensive support for 'Free Rides'—allowing users to record sessions and control their smart trainer without a pre-defined workout. It also refactors the entire Workout Tab into a unified **Dashboard & Cockpit** UX for a professional, cohesive experience across all ride modes and devices.

### Key Features
* **Free Ride Mode:** Start a session directly from setup. Support for live **Resistance**, **Power (ERG)**, and **Heart Rate (ERG)** manual controls.
* **Unified Cockpit UI:** Refactored interaction zone at the bottom of the screen. Muscle memory is now preserved between modes: toggling ERG and adjusting intensity always happens in the same 'Thumb Zone.'
* **Shielded Row Control Cluster:** A safe, centralized adjustment panel. Large primary buttons for fine increments (+/- 1) are flanked by smaller, 'shielded' coarse adjustment buttons (+/- 10/5) separated by a 20pt safety gutter.
* **Dynamic Session Graphs:** New 'SessionGraphView' that scales in real-time. Features include X-axis time reference labels and a unified legend shared with structured workouts.
* **iPad Reliability:** Refactored 'DataFieldGrid' to use an adaptive layout, fixing clipping issues on large iPad screens (e.g., iPad Pro 13-inch).

### Fixes & Improvements
* **FitEncoder Stability:** Fixed a crash caused by heart rate or cadence values exceeding 255 (UInt8 overflow).
* **Realistic Simulation:** Capped simulated heart rate in 'SimulatedPeripheral' to prevent unrealistic spikes and data errors.
* **Enhanced Previews:** High-fidelity SwiftUI previews for both 'Free Ride' and 'Structured Workout' scenarios.

### Testing Done

* Confirmed graph scaling and label visibility over long simulated durations.

author: lawzava
body:
💡 **What:** 
Removed the `JSON.parse` and `JSON.stringify` logic inside the persistence fallback blocks in `handleEdit` and `handleDelete` in `src/routes/[roomId]/+page.svelte`.

🎯 **Why:** 
The fallback mechanism was parsing and stringifying the entire `chatHistory_{roomId}` string from `localStorage`. For large chat histories (e.g., 10k messages), this caused massive performance overhead (measuring >2.5s locally for a block of edits) and scaled poorly. The WASM module contains the exact state and has a `saveRoomMessagesToStorage` method. If WASM fails to edit the message, it means the message isn't in the WASM state, and trying to force it into localStorage is a bad idea because the next time the page loads, WASM will load it from localStorage, but right now WASM and UI are out of sync. Removing the fallback allows the application to rely purely on WASM state sync and accept a local-only optimistic update if it fails, which is vastly more resilient and efficient.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Based on a local micro-benchmark simulating 10,000 messages and 100 sequential edit operations:
*   **Baseline:** 2618ms
*   **Without fallback (Optimized):** ~5ms
*   **Improvement:** 99.8% reduction in execution time for the edge-case fallback path.

author: arian81
body:
### TL;DR

Added automatic tagging of the latest commit with `vscode-extension-latest` tag during the VS Code extension release workflow.

### What changed?

The GitHub workflow now includes a step that moves the `vscode-extension-latest` tag to point to the current commit and force pushes it to the remote repository. This happens after the release artifacts are uploaded but before updating the latest release.

### How to test?

Trigger the VS Code extension release workflow and verify that:
1. The `vscode-extension-latest` tag is created/updated to point to the release commit
2. The tag is successfully pushed to the remote repository
3. The workflow completes without errors

### Why make this change?

This ensures there's always a stable reference point (`vscode-extension-latest` tag) that points to the most recent VS Code extension release, making it easier for users and automated systems to reference the latest stable version.

author: oguyon
body:
## Summary

Identifies and fixes all sites where `createimagefromIMGID()` or `imcreateIMGID()` was being called inside real-time compute loops, causing shared-memory allocation on every frame.

## Root cause

`createimagefromIMGID()` has **no idempotency guard** — it unconditionally calls `create_image_ID()` every time, performing a SHM lookup and potential `mmap` on every frame. `imcreateIMGID()` is guarded (via `imcreatelikewiseIMGID`), but still incurs branch + function-call overhead when placed inside the hot path.

## Changes

### 🔴 High priority — unguarded `createimagefromIMGID` per frame

| File | Fix |
|------|-----|
| `SGEMM.c` | Add `if (outimg->ID == -1)` guard — output matrix was being reallocated every frame |
| `extract_RGGBchan.c` | Move 4 output IMGIDs before loop; change function to pointer signature; add `if (ID == -1)` guard for each channel |

### 🟠 Medium priority — unguarded `createimagefromIMGID` per frame

| File | Fix |
|------|-----|
| `image_mk_reim_from_complex.c` | Add `if (ID == -1)` guards (2 datatype branches × 2 outputs) |
| `image_mk_amph_from_complex.c` | Add `if (ID == -1)` guards (2 datatype branches × 2 outputs) |
| `image_mk_complex_from_amph.c` | Add `if (ID == -1)` guards (4 datatype branches) |

### 🟡 Low priority — `imcreateIMGID` in hot loop (guarded but wasted overhead)

| File | Fix |
|------|-----|
| `examplefunc4_streamprocess.c` | Move `imcreateIMGID` from `streamprocess()` to `compute_function()` before `INIT` macro |
| `im3D_to_stream2D.c` | Move `imcreateIMGID` before `INIT` macro; also **fix pre-existing bug** where `extract_slice_to_2D()` was called **twice per frame** |

## Testing

Build passes cleanly with zero errors or warnings on all 7 modified files.

body:
Implement a generic vhost-user frontend device that is agnostic to the specific virtio device type being emulated. Unlike per-device-type frontends, this device delegates config space ownership entirely to the backend via the mandatory CONFIG protocol feature, allowing any virtio device type (e.g. virtio-fs, virtio-scsi) to be used without a
dedicated Firecracker frontend.

A VirtioDeviceType::VhostUserGeneric sentinel (0xFF) serves as the host-side MMIO map key, while a new mmio_device_type_id() trait method returns the real virtio type ID to the guest MMIO register. Queue count
is dynamic (Vec) since different device types need different configurations. Snapshotting is stubbed out, consistent with the existing vhost-user block device.

The device is configured via PUT /vhost-user-devices/{id} and tested end-to-end with virtiofsd — guest kernel recognises the device with the correct virtio type ID.

Closes #5687

author: jrf0110
body:
## Summary

- **Three failure paths in `processReviewQueue()`** (no rig_id, no rig config, container fails to start) were calling `reviewQueue.completeReview()` directly — a raw SQL UPDATE that bypasses `updateBeadStatus()`, skipping convoy progress updates and leaving source beads stuck in `in_review` permanently. Replaced all three with a new `failReviewWithRework()` helper that routes through `completeReviewWithResult()`, which properly logs events, updates convoy progress, returns the source bead to `in_progress`, and dispatches a polecat for rework.
- **Added `recoverOrphanedSourceBeads()`** — a safety-net recovery function (called each alarm cycle) that detects source beads stuck in `in_review` whose MR bead has already reached a terminal state, and returns them to `in_progress`.
- **Fixed bead status rollback in `dispatchAgent()`** — the `!started` (container failed) path was rolling back the agent to `idle` but leaving the bead in `in_progress`. Now rolls back the bead to `open` (consistent with the `throw` path), making the retry via `schedulePendingWork` more predictable.

Closes #1243

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — passes
- [x] `pnpm lint` (gastown) — passes
- [x] `pnpm test:integration` — all new tests pass (5/5); 1 pre-existing failure in `convoy-dag.test.ts` unrelated to this change
- [x] Verified the pre-existing test failure (`should include merge_mode in review queue metadata for convoy beads`) reproduces on `main`

## Visual Changes

N/A

## Reviewer Notes

- The `completeReview()` function in `review-queue.ts` still exists and is still called internally by `completeReviewWithResult()` — it's the low-level SQL update. The fix ensures no caller in `processReviewQueue` uses it directly for failure paths.
- `recoverOrphanedSourceBeads` uses the same 5-minute timeout as `recoverStuckReviews`. It only recovers beads whose MR bead is already in a terminal state (`closed`/`failed`), so it won't interfere with in-flight reviews.
- The `dispatchAgent` bead rollback fix may be a no-op in fire-and-forget contexts (the I/O gate may already be closed per the existing comment at line 2982), but it ensures correct behavior when `dispatchAgent` is awaited directly (as in `processReviewQueue`).

Large-scale deduplication and complexity reduction across the entire VelesDB workspace. This PR targets Codacy compliance (CC ≤ 8, NLOC ≤ 50/fn, ≤ 500/file) by extracting shared helpers, splitting oversized files into module directories, and eliminating copy-paste patterns.

body:
The XLL had several issues preventing correct loading and function execution in Excel: a C++17 compile break, missing `DllMain` for TLS, a silent validation no-op, and a bounds-unsafe string check.

## Fixes

- **`std::auto_ptr` → `std::unique_ptr<char[]>`** (`XlOpenClose.cpp`)  
  `auto_ptr` is removed in C++17; modern MSVC builds failed to compile. Replaced with `unique_ptr<char[]>`.

- **Add `DllMain`** (`XlOpenClose.cpp`)  
  `TLS_Action()` in `mgw/TLS.cpp` was never called — `TlsIndex` stayed uninitialized, causing UB on any multi-threaded Excel calc path. `DllMain` now delegates to it:
  ```cpp
  BOOL WINAPI DllMain(HINSTANCE hinstDLL, DWORD fdwReason, LPVOID lpvReserved)
  {
      return TLS_Action(fdwReason);
  }
  ```

- **Fix `DividendsTable_Create` validation** (`cpp_iface/justatest.cpp`)  
  `aExDivDates.Size() != aExDivDates.Size()` is a tautology — size mismatch between ex-div and payment date vectors was never caught. Fixed to compare against `aPaymentDates.Size()`.

- **Fix `IsMGObjectDescriptor` length guard** (`xlw/cache/cached.cpp`)  
  `size() == 14` is a no-op (no valid descriptor is 14 chars). For strings shorter than 6 chars, `at(5)` throws `out_of_range`. Replaced with `size() < 16`, matching the minimum valid format `XXXXX_1_HH:MM:SS`.

body:
This PR adds a simple, rule-based AI Director directly into the browser to autonomously control NPC agents. It satisfies the request to run a simple AI in the browser without the overhead of downloading and running a heavy local LLM model in WebAssembly.

The AI logic uses the existing `window.GenieAI` API to poll NPC states (`getNPCState`) and issue movement and chat commands (`commandNPC`) based on the `player_distance`. It is toggled via a new UI button in the Controls panel.

A Playwright test has been included to ensure the toggle button functions correctly.

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced `parsed_df.apply(generate_peptides, axis=1)` with a list comprehension over `parsed_df.itertuples(index=False)` in `mutated_genes.py`. Updated `generate_peptides` in `helper_functions.py` to use direct attribute access (`row.pos`, `getattr(row, 'end_pos', pos)`) instead of dictionary access/`.get()` fallbacks. Adapted unit tests to mock `itertuples` namedtuples correctly. Cleaned up unused imports. Added critical learnings to `.jules/bolt.md`.

🎯 **Why:** Pandas `apply(axis=1)` has massive overhead due to the continuous creation of `pd.Series` objects. Utilizing `itertuples(index=False)` yields lightweight namedtuples which drastically reduces processing time.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** Reduces row processing time in `mutated_genes.py` by approximately ~6x (0.3s instead of 1.9s on 50k rows in local benchmarking).

🔬 **Measurement:** Verify by running `uv run process_data.py` on the TCGA mutation datasets or by running a generic profiling script over `process_mutations_in_batches`.

author: tikazyq
body:
## Summary

Replace AI subagent calls with classical algorithms for all structurally-decidable operations in fractal decomposition. This implements the "AI for semantics, algorithms for structure" principle, reducing AI calls by ~40% while improving determinism, reproducibility, and cost.

## Key Changes

- **Decompose Gate** (`cli/src/fractal/decompose.rs`): 
  - TF-IDF weighted cosine similarity for orthogonality checking (via `rust-tfidf` crate)
  - Kahn's topological sort for dependency cycle detection
  - Weighted feature scoring for complexity estimation
  - Proportional budget allocation by complexity score
  - Coverage analysis via set difference

- **Solve Scheduler** (`cli/src/fractal/schedule.rs`):
  - DAG-based critical path scheduling using BFS layer decomposition
  - Computes parallel execution waves from dependency graph
  - Longest-path DP for critical path analysis
  - Replaces binary parallel/sequential choice with optimal scheduling

- **Reunify Merge** (`cli/src/fractal/reunify.rs`):
  - 3-way merge via `git merge-tree` for code reunification
  - Structural conflict detection: boundary violations, redundant files, interface gaps
  - Set intersection analysis for scope violations
  - Auto-resolution of structural conflicts without AI

- **Prune Gate** (`cli/src/fractal/prune.rs`):
  - Greedy set cover approximation for minimal covering set
  - Subset analysis for output containment detection
  - Identity detection for duplicate outputs
  - File coverage mapping

- **CLI Integration** (`cli/src/cmd/fractal.rs`, `cli/src/main.rs`):
  - New `synodic fractal` command with subcommands: `gate`, `schedule`, `reunify`, `prune`, `complexity`
  - JSON stdin/stdout interface for integration with orchestration layer
  - Standalone complexity scoring pre-filter

- **Documentation** (`docs/FRACTAL.md`, `specs/047-fractal-algorithmic-spine/README.md`):
  - Comprehensive guide to fractal decomposition with algorithmic spine
  - Detailed algorithm descriptions and classical analogs
  - Orchestration protocol and configuration reference
  - AI vs algorithm split visualization

- **Shared Types** (`cli/src/fractal/mod.rs`):
  - Common data structures for decompose, schedule, reunify, prune gates
  - Term extraction utilities (Jaccard similarity, term set operations)

## Implementation Details

- **Term Extraction**: Regex-based extraction of 3+ char alphanumeric terms with stop-word filtering
- **TF-IDF**: Uses `rust-tfidf` crate for proper inverse document frequency weighting; discriminative terms get higher weight than ubiquitous ones
- **Cycle Detection**: Kahn's algorithm with in-degree tracking; O(V+E) complexity
- **Scheduling**: Topological sort into waves; critical path computed via DP on longest dependency chain
- **Set Cover**: Greedy approximation with O(ln n) ratio guarantee
- **Thresholds**: Jaccard > 30% OR TF-IDF cosine > 30% for orthogonality flags; coverage < 80% for coverage flags

All operations are deterministic and reproducible, with no randomness or external state dependencies.

### Motivation
- Live session backfill and quant backtests were producing incomplete or misaligned market inputs because live hydration only used stored trades and backtests relied on sparse trade-only feeds. 
- The goal is to restore deterministic live chart/backtest parity by feeding both live and backtests from the same canonical minute-candle inputs derived from Binance 1m klines.

### Description
- Add a reusable Binance historical helper `server/binanceHistoricalData.js` that paginates 1m klines and derives canonical minute candles, kline-based CVD, and aggressor (buy/sell) buckets. 
- Seed live-session hydration with canonical candles and derived CVD/aggressor buckets at startup and change live replay to use the hydrated canonical session state (`server/index.js`).
- Switch backtests to request canonical market-data (`loadMarketData`) from Binance klines with a stored-trades fallback, make `BacktestRunner.run` async and returned to the job service (`server/quant/backtestRunner.js`, `server/quant/backtestJobService.js`).
- Add/extend tests to validate kline-derived inputs and that backtests execute from both trade-driven and canonical inputs (`server/binanceHistoricalData.test.js`, updated `server/quant/replayOrchestrator.test.js`).

### Testing
- Ran unit tests: `node --test server/quant/*.test.js server/binanceHistoricalData.test.js` and all tests passed (10/10 subtests + new kline helper test). 
- Verified frontend build: `npm run build` completed successfully.

body:
# Description

GCC enables `-Wsign-compare` by default but CLANG does not enable `-Wsign-compare` by default. This causes GCC unit test builds to fail with a signed/unsigned mismatch when using googletest macros `EXPECT_EQ()`, `ASSERT_EQ()`, `EXPECT_NE()`, or `ASSERT_NE()` with one of the operands being literal 0. However, CLANG does not fail for these builds.

Add `-Wsign-compare` to `CXX_FLAGS` for `CLANGDWARF` and `CLANGPDB` to align CLANG error checking with GCC.

Add `/w44388` and `/w44389` to MSFT family compiler `CXX_FLAGS` to align VS20xx error checking with GCC.

Add unit tests that use `EXPECT_EQ()`, `ASSERT_EQ()`, `EXPECT_NE()`, and `ASSERT_NE()` to check a local variables of type `UINTN`, `UINT8`, `UINT16`, `UINT32`, `UINT64`, `UINT32` bitfields, and `UINT64` bitfields against literal 0 values.

- [ ] Breaking change?
- [ ] Impacts security?
- [ ] Includes tests?

## How This Was Tested

Added unit tests that pass for CLANG and MSFT but fail for GCC.  Added options to make sure CLANG, MSFT, and GCC catch the same errors.  Then update unit tests to pass CLANG, MSFT, and GCC.

## Integration Instructions

If unit test failures in CLANG or MSFT are generated by this change but same unit tests pass GCC, then replace `0` with `0u` in `EXPECT_EQ()`, `ASSERT_EQ()`, `EXPECT_NE()`, or `ASSERT_NE()` statements referenced in build logs.

### Motivation
- Reduce production serial I/O overhead and centralize log formatting by replacing ad-hoc `Serial.print/println` calls with a leveled logging wrapper. 
- Provide a global switch and log level so debug output can be disabled or filtered for production devices.

### Description
- Add `serial_logging.h` which provides `serial_log_print(level, ...)`, `serial_log_printf(level, ...)`, log level enum (`ERROR`, `WARN`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`) and runtime checks. 
- Add logging configuration in `config.h` with `#define ACTIVE_LOGS 1` and `#define LOG_LEVEL INFO` so logs can be turned off or filtered; default log level is `INFO`.
- Migrate application serial output to the wrapper (set to `INFO` by default) across main sources: `telelogger.cpp`, `teleclient.cpp`, `telestore.cpp`, `dataserver.cpp`, and `CAN-uds.cpp` so all printed messages respect the new logging policy. 
- Use `serial_log_printf(...)` for formatted lines and `serial_log_print(...)` for other messages and string/variable printing, preserving original message content and adding level prefixes.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` to verify no trailing-whitespace/apply_patch issues; this check succeeded. 
- Ran repository search (`rg`) to confirm `Serial.print/println` usages were migrated to `serial_log_*` in the targeted files. 
- Attempted to build with `platformio run` and `python -m platformio run` but `platformio` is not available in this environment so a full compile was not executed. 
- Committed the changes after local verification of the diffs and replacements succeeded.
